campaigns.name: Campaigns of the Adventuring Age
campaigns.summary: A dossier index for the Northrend war and the later world-to-world campaign against the Burning Legion.

campaigns.name: Ancient Kalimdor Conflicts
campaigns.summary: A research grouping for the long wars that redistributed peoples and power before kaldorei ascendance, beginning with the supported troll–aqir campaign.

campaigns.name: The Elemental Resistance to the Black Empire
campaigns.summary: A descriptive campaign grouping for the Elemental Lords' united attempt to remove the Old Gods and their growing empire.

campaigns.name: The Elemental Wars
campaigns.summary: A descriptive campaign grouping for the prolonged struggle among Azeroth's four elemental hosts.

campaigns.name: Wars of a Wounded World
campaigns.summary: A dossier index for the Fourth War and the assaults surrounding N'Zoth's release.

campaigns.name: Conflicts of the Post-Sundering Kingdoms
campaigns.summary: An atlas-scale grouping for the two best-supported conflicts that materially redistributed power during Era 5: the Troll Wars and the War of the Three Hammers.

campaigns.name: The Rise of the Horde and the First Two Wars
campaigns.summary: A cross-world strategic grouping from the Horde's formation and draenei war through the First and Second Wars, ending with the Old Horde's defeat and destruction of the original Dark Portal.

campaigns.name: The Third War and the Frozen Throne
campaigns.summary: A strategic grouping of the coalition defense at Mount Hyjal and the later cross-world contest that ended at the Frozen Throne.

campaigns.name: The Titan-forged War for Azeroth
campaigns.summary: An editorial campaign grouping for the keeper-led war that broke the Black Empire and made containment and planetary repair possible.

campaigns.name: The War of the Ancients Campaign
campaigns.summary: A strategic grouping of the Legion invasion, the widening defense of Kalimdor, the betrayal of Neltharion, and the final convergence at the Well.

eras.name: The Age of Adventurers

startDate.label: Early renewed adventuring campaigns after the Frozen Throne

endDate.label: The end of the Argus campaign and the Legion's immediate crusade

eras.dateLabel: Ahn'Qiraj through Argus · sequence established, exact dating under review
eras.summary: The age in which expeditions and champions repeatedly crossed the world's thresholds: Ahn'Qiraj, Outland, Northrend, the Cataclysm, Pandaria, alternate Draenor, the Broken Isles, and Argus.

eras.name: Rise of the Ancient Civilizations

startDate.label: About 16,000 years before the Dark Portal

endDate.label: Before the War of the Ancients

eras.dateLabel: c. 16,000–10,000 years before the Dark Portal · research chronology
eras.summary: The first troll powers, the war with the aqir, the rise and fall of the mogu empire, and the ascent of the kaldorei around the Well of Eternity.

eras.name: Primordial Azeroth and the Black Empire
eras.summary: Azeroth's immense nascent world-soul left its native elementals without enough Spirit to balance them. Their long conflict was overtaken by the arrival of the Old Gods and the civilization their servants raised across the primordial world.

eras.name: Cosmic Origins
eras.dateLabel: Before the ordering of worlds · chronology without measured dates
eras.summary: The cited account begins with Light and Shadow, the birth of the physical universe and Twisting Nether, the awakening of world-souls, the gathering of the titan Pantheon, and the Void Lords' attempt to corrupt a nascent titan through the Old Gods.

eras.name: The Long Vigil and the New Kingdoms

startDate.label: After the Great Sundering, approximately 10,000 years before the Dark Portal

endDate.label: Before the rise of the Horde and the opening of the Dark Portal

eras.dateLabel: c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal to the centuries immediately preceding it · research chronology
eras.summary: The kaldorei begin the Long Vigil while migrations, alliances, wars, and political fragmentation establish Quel'Thalas, Arathor's successor kingdoms, and the divided powers of Khaz Modan.

eras.name: The Modern Cosmic Age

endDate.label: Ongoing; archive includes the released Curse of Ula’tek chapter (August 2026)

eras.dateLabel: Fourth War through Curse of Ula’tek · ongoing archive
eras.summary: A wounded world passes through the Fourth War, N’Zoth, the Shadowlands, the Dragon Isles, Khaz Algar, shattered K’aresh, and the released Midnight crisis in Quel’Thalas. Later Worldsoul Saga outcomes remain open.

eras.name: Ordering of Azeroth
eras.dateLabel: After the Black Empire · before the rise of ancient civilizations
eras.summary: The Pantheon intervenes to save Azeroth, the keeper-led titan-forged break the Black Empire, the surviving Old Gods are imprisoned, and the wounded world is stabilized and reshaped.

eras.name: The Rise of the Horde and the First Two Wars

startDate.label: Approximately thirteen years before the opening of the Dark Portal; working chronology

endDate.label: At the end of the Second War; working chronology

eras.dateLabel: c. 13 years before the Dark Portal through the end of the Second War · research chronology
eras.summary: Draenor's corruption, the orcs' fall to the Legion, opening of the Dark Portal, destruction of Stormwind, and the Alliance victory in the Second War.

eras.name: The Third War and the Frozen Throne

endDate.label: Arthas's ascent at the Frozen Throne; working chronology

eras.dateLabel: c. 20–22 years after the Dark Portal · research chronology
eras.summary: The Scourge, Arthas's downfall, destruction of Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas, the Legion's return, the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and the creation of the Lich King's new order.

eras.name: The War of the Ancients and the Sundering

startDate.label: c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal

endDate.label: The Great Sundering, c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal

eras.dateLabel: c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal · research chronology
eras.summary: Political choices around the Well enabled the Burning Legion's first invasion, drew defenders from across ancient Kalimdor, and ended with the Great Sundering.

entities.name: Aggramar
entities.shortDescription: The titan who discovered the imperiled world of Azeroth and urged the Pantheon to act through purpose-built servants rather than overwhelming force.
entities.body: Aggramar recognized both the promise of Azeroth's sleeping world-soul and the danger posed by the Black Empire. Blizzard's first-party account emphasizes his concern that the Pantheon's colossal intervention could destroy what they meant to save.

entities.name: The Amani Empire
entities.shortDescription: The forest-troll power whose ancestral northern lands came into conflict with Quel'Thalas and later Arathor.
entities.body: The Amani were an organized forest-troll people with ancestral ties to the northern lands. The founding of Quel'Thalas brought them into conflict with the high elves, and that struggle later drew Arathor into the Troll Wars.

entities.name: Aman’Thul
entities.shortDescription: The first titan to awaken in the cited account, who crossed the Great Dark in search of others of his kind.
entities.body: Aman’Thul's search gathered the awakened titans into the Pantheon. When the Pantheon confronted the corruption on Azeroth, his direct removal of Y'Shaarj revealed how deeply the Old Gods had rooted themselves in the world.

entities.name: Aqir
entities.shortDescription: Resilient insectoid servants formed from the Old Gods' organic matter, first set to building the Black Empire and later drawn into a world-spanning war with the ancient troll powers.
entities.body: The aqir first served the Old Gods in the building of the Black Empire. After their war with the ancient troll powers, surviving groups retreated in different directions and gave rise to separate northern and southern societies.

entities.name: Arathor
entities.shortDescription: The first great human nation, united under Thoradin and centered at Strom.
entities.body: Thoradin united early human communities under Arathor, with Strom as its center. That union gave the human kingdoms a shared political origin, though the realm later divided into separate states.

entities.body: The Forge worked in concert with the northern Forge of Wills. Its public overview states both its healing purpose and its terrible contingency without suggesting that the latter was used during this era.

entities.name: Forge of Souls

entities.name: The Frozen Halls
entities.shortDescription: A group of Icecrown dungeon wings comprising the Forge of Souls, Pit of Saron and Halls of Reflection. The quest-item drop is randomized gameplay, not a singular event with a known finder.

entities.name: The Frozen Throne
entities.shortDescription: The prison and seat of the Lich King at Icecrown, reached by Arthas after his victory over Illidan.

entities.name: The Highborne Exiles
entities.shortDescription: The arcane-practicing Highborne who left Kalimdor and eventually established a new homeland in the east.
entities.body: The record follows a migrating population across a long and incompletely measured journey. Its route is deliberately simplified, and the generated family-and-scholar group avoids presenting the migration as only a military expedition.

entities.name: The Highborne
entities.shortDescription: The privileged kaldorei arcanists around Azshara whose ritual at the Well opened the way for the Burning Legion.
entities.body: This dossier treats the court collectively so the tour can explain institutional choice without inventing a complete roster. The figure and its placement are original interpretive representations, not a palace plan or licensed art.

entities.name: Horde party
entities.shortDescription: Horde party, an interpretive group representing one viewpoint in a separate faction quest path.
entities.body: Original interpretive AI-generated artwork, not canonical game art or evidence for a costume, location or event. See the storyline production and visual ledgers for the evidence boundary.

entities.name: The Defenders of Mount Hyjal
entities.shortDescription: A temporary coalition of night elves, Horde forces, Alliance survivors, and their leaders assembled against the Legion's advance.
entities.body: This grouping describes cooperation in one existential defense; it does not erase the distinct peoples, commands, or conflicts within it.

entities.body: This research record stays within the war itself and does not import Illidan's later appearance or identity into the ancient map. The portrait therefore omits the signs of his later demonic transformation. For the Age of Adventurers, the map renderer uses a separate era-specific figure of Illidan in Outland while preserving this ancient portrait as the default.

entities.name: Ironforge

entities.shortDescription: The civilization that arose around the Well of Eternity, mastered its arcane energies, and expanded swiftly across ancient Kalimdor.
entities.body: The kaldorei grew powerful around the Well of Eternity through their mastery of its arcane energies. Their rapid expansion changed the balance among the ancient peoples of Kalimdor and set the stage for the empire that faced the War of the Ancients.

entities.name: Kalecgos

entities.body: Kang's importance lies not in a single mapped duel but in a method that could spread among a disarmed people. The figure is therefore placed relationally beside the southern uprising rather than assigned an exact battlefield.

events.name: The War Effort Opens Ahn'Qiraj

date.label: Early in the age of adventurers

events.summary: Alliance and Horde communities supplied a shared war effort before champions entered Ahn'Qiraj to confront C'Thun's forces.
events.description: The record preserves the unusual scale of cooperation without reconstructing server-specific contributions or raid tactics.

events.name: Akama and Maiev

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: Akama explains the bargain behind the display. Illidan’s rule has made open revolt a danger to the Broken, so the plan must grow in secret. Maiev Shadowsong is imprisoned in Akama’s hidden quarters. She is no obedient instrument in his designs: her anger at Illidan and her own choices remain hers. Their uneasy meeting turns the chamber into a question of agency as well as escape.

events.name: Akama’s promise to A’dal

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: In Shattrath, Akama places the Heart within the Medallion of Karabor and sends it to A’dal. His promise is to stand with the seeker against Illidan; this closes the first Akama chain. The medallion links Karabor’s sacred name to a dangerous plan, but its delivery does not open the raid or free Akama’s soul. The harder struggle still waits inside the Black Temple.

events.name: Beneath the Warden’s Cage

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: At the Warden’s Cage, a submerged pool hides a chamber beyond the outpost. There the seeker finds Akama, no longer merely a name in another commander’s orders. At this meeting the question changes: the search has found the leader, but his place beside Illidan still conceals what he means to do.

events.name: A diversion at the southern wall

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: Entry comes by a raid-scale diversion. Xi’ri and the Sha’tar draw Illidan’s defenders outward while Akama, Maiev and the Deathsworn move on the fortress. Maiev pursues her own vengeance, and Akama continues with his people when she breaks from the plan. At the southern wall they pass through an opening; the account leaves the rest of the temple’s defences untold.

events.name: The fall of the Betrayer

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: At last, Akama and the adventurers face Illidan atop the Black Temple. The Betrayer’s fall ends the Burning Crusade quest that carried the seeker from Baa’ri through the raids and into the fortress. Akama has reclaimed his soul, and the Ashtongue have risen from Illidan’s control. The tale leaves Karabor’s later fate and Akama’s rule unspoken.

events.name: The Heart of Fury

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: At Ata’mal Terrace, the seeker recovers the Heart of Fury. Akama recognizes it from Velen’s past and weighs the power it might give him against his people’s freedom. The quest account makes his choice clear: he will not free the Broken only to take Illidan’s place as their master. He sends the artifact onward to A’dal. This refusal gives the hidden plan its clearest purpose.

events.name: The hostage soul

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: When the phylactery returns to Akama, its power over souls makes his design plain: his own soul is imprisoned in the Black Temple, apart from the leader his people see. He intends to reclaim control of it before facing Illidan. The discovery makes this long deception personal without erasing its wider stakes. The quest records a plan and an intended use, not certainty that the artifact will succeed.

events.name: A memory at Mount Hyjal

date.label: Third War battle represented as a Caverns of Time memory; the quest instance is later, exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: Akama seeks the Time-Phased Phylactery once held by Rage Winterchill. The path sends the adventurer into the Caverns of Time and a memory of the Battle of Mount Hyjal, where the artifact is recovered. This is not present-day travel from Outland into the Third War. A separate raid attunement is required to enter Hyjal; that gate is a game condition, not the cause of Akama’s plan.

events.name: Karabor under Illidan

date.label: Before the Burning Crusade; Illidan’s seizure of Karabor is described retrospectively, exact date unknown

events.summary: Before a black name crowned the height, Karabor was the draenei’s sacred temple in Shadowmoon Valley. War and occupation stripped that name from its halls; the fortress became the Black Temple. Illidan seized it from Magtheridon, and the Broken under Akama joined his ranks. Their public allegiance did not reveal Akama’s private purpose. The quests that begin among Baa’ri’s tablets enter this inherited history, then ask what it has cost his people.

events.name: The secret is found

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: After the first chain and a separate raid gate, Seer Olum appears in Serpentshrine Cavern. He tells the seeker that Vashj’s followers uncovered the Deathsworn’s secret and tortured him for it. This is an access-dependent encounter in the Burning Crusade quest order, not proof that the raid gate caused Akama’s conspiracy. Olum has kept silent; now the plan is endangered, and Akama must choose what one friend can bear.

events.name: Olum’s last choice

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: At the Warden’s Cage, Olum chooses the spirit world rather than risk giving his captors the secret. Akama helps him die among his brothers. Illidan’s suspicion then demands another act: Akama reports a genuine betrayal by Kael’thas, diverting attention from the Ashtongue plot. Olum’s sacrifice leaves no triumph in its wake. It preserves the cover at the cost of one of the plan’s oldest companions.

events.name: Orders and fragments

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: From the ruins, Oronu’s written orders and the Ashtongue shamans redirect the seeker through the valley. Their quest steps recover pieces of the Medallion of Karabor and lead deeper toward Akama. The targets and collection count are player progress, not a census of the tribe or a chain of distinct battles. The trail is valuable because it reveals that an apparent servant of Illidan has left instructions in trusted hands.

events.name: Proof of Allegiance

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: Access to Akama is followed by a test of loyalty. The quest directs the seeker against Ashtongue whom Akama marks as a threat to his cover. This violence belongs to a controlled performance within the chain: his Deathsworn remain the trusted circle while his public service to Illidan is maintained. The objective is not evidence of a massacre of the tribe or that Akama has abandoned his people.

events.name: Ruse of the Ashtongue

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: The ruse is tested in Tempest Keep. Wearing an Ashtongue Cowl, the seeker kills Al’ar, Kael’thas’s phoenix, under the appearance of obeying Illidan. The chain calls for this deed after Olum’s death because Akama needs Illidan to trust the outward story again. It is a raid task used to preserve a disguise, not evidence that the Ashtongue have openly begun their assault.

events.name: Find the Ashtongue

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: Inside the Black Temple, the seeker finds Akama’s Deathsworn and Seer Kanai. Their message is simple: Akama needs help. The campaign has crossed from a concealed valley plan to a confrontation within Illidan’s fortress. The Ashtongue have not yet escaped his influence; their leader’s soul remains bound, and the next task is to break that hold before the people can turn together.

events.name: Seer Udalo in the Arcatraz

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: The next search leads to the Arcatraz, a crystalline prison suspended above Netherstorm. The seeker is sent to find Seer Udalo and discovers that the seer is already dead. The quest offers no return from death here; Akama receives a report and sends the seeker onward. A keeper of the Ashtongue secret has fallen far from Shadowmoon, leaving the living to interpret what he managed to leave behind.

events.name: The Shade of Akama

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: With help from the adventurers, Akama defeats his Shade and reclaims the soul held apart from him. The Ashtongue turn from Illidan’s sway; the blow against the Betrayer begins within the tribe before it reaches the summit. Open resistance had seemed too dangerous for a people already brought close to ruin. The story marks a change in agency, not a claim that every Broken in Outland has joined the same revolt.

events.name: Tablets at Baa’ri

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: The attunement begins at Baa’ri: a trail of tablets, orders and medallion fragments leads from Shadowmoon toward Akama. Aldor and Scryers receive different opening quests from their own camps; those alternatives later converge. They are not one adventurer’s combined route. The tablets and collection objectives open a path through the valley, but they do not establish that every fragment records a separate historical act.

events.name: The seers open the way

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: After the Council, the spirits of Udalo and Olum open the way to Illidan’s sanctum. Their work has not been forgotten: one left the word that led Akama toward Ata’mal; the other gave his life to guard the hidden plan. Now both seers act beyond death. The other trials fade from view as their purpose brings the company to Illidan’s door.

events.name: The word Ata’mal

date.label: Burning Crusade quest chronology; exact in-world dating unknown

events.summary: Udalo left only a single word, Ata’mal, on the floor. Akama reads it as the next place to seek. No fuller prophecy survives in the available quest record, and this fragment cannot bear more certainty than it contains. A name passes from the prison into the valley’s old temple terraces; the slender clue is enough to move the story, but not enough to reveal what waits there.

events.name: The Alliance of Lordaeron Forms

date.label: After Stormwind's fall and before the Second War

events.summary: Stormwind's warning and the approaching Horde threat drew human kingdoms and allied peoples into a military coalition centered on Lordaeron.

events.name: The Allied Powers Defeat the Amani

date.label: At the conclusion of the Troll Wars

events.summary: The combined high-elven and human campaign broke the immediate Amani offensive and sharply reduced the empire's regional power without ending the Amani people.

events.name: Awakening of Aman’Thul

date.label: After worlds formed within the Great Dark

events.summary: Aman’Thul awoke from the world that had nurtured his spirit and began searching the cosmos for other nascent titans.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the sequence described in Chronicle Volume 1.

events.name: The Aqir Awaken

date.label: After the early troll powers had spread

events.summary: Ancient aqir forces emerged again and pressed into troll-held lands, turning scattered rivalry into a shared existential danger.

events.name: The Aqir Successor Powers Emerge

date.label: After the long troll pursuit

events.summary: Separated aqir populations entrenched themselves in distant refuges, producing new northern and southern powers rather than restoring one united dominion.

events.name: Arathor Fragments into the Seven Kingdoms

date.label: By approximately 1,200 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Over generations, Arathor's distant city-states became sovereign powers and the unified human empire gave way to seven kingdoms.

events.name: Archimonde Is Destroyed at Mount Hyjal

date.label: At the climax of the Third War

events.summary: The defenders delayed Archimonde until Malfurion released Nordrassil's gathered power, destroying the Legion commander and repelling the assault.

events.name: Archimonde Is Summoned into Azeroth

date.label: After the northern kingdoms are broken

events.summary: The Scourge's campaign opened the way for Archimonde and the Burning Legion to return and turn their advance toward Kalimdor and Nordrassil.

events.name: The Campaign Reaches Argus

date.label: At the culmination of the Legion campaign

events.summary: A direct link carried the coalition to shattered Argus and the Burning Legion's seat of power.

events.name: Arthas Ascends the Frozen Throne

date.label: At the close of the Frozen Throne campaign

events.summary: After defeating Illidan, Arthas reached the Frozen Throne and joined with the Lich King, establishing the new order that closes this era.

events.name: Arthas Claims Frostmourne

date.label: During Arthas's Northrend pursuit

events.summary: Arthas pursued the Scourge into Northrend and took up Frostmourne, a choice that bound his fate more tightly to the Lich King.

events.name: Azeroth Is Ordered

date.label: After the world-forges were established

events.summary: The titan-forged raised mountains, opened waterways, dredged seas, maintained great works, and helped make the wounded world stable enough for life to flourish.

events.name: Azshara Rises to the Throne

date.label: Near the height of prewar kaldorei power

events.summary: Azshara became queen of a powerful kaldorei civilization whose court and arcane ambitions stood at the threshold of the next catastrophe.

events.name: Black Empire Dominion

date.label: After the elemental resistance failed

events.summary: The elementals failed to dislodge the Old Gods and were enslaved; without that resistance, Black Empire influence extended over much of the world.

events.name: Rise of the Black Empire

date.label: After the Old Gods' arrival

events.summary: The n'raqi directed the aqir in building citadels and temple cities around the Old Gods; Y'Shaarj's central bastion became the greatest of these domains as their holdings spread.

events.name: The Legion's Crusade Is Broken

date.label: At the end of the Argus campaign

events.summary: The Argus campaign broke the Burning Legion's immediate cosmic crusade, closing the era with victory and a wounded world left behind.

events.name: The Class Orders Rise Against the Legion

date.label: During the Legion's return

events.summary: As the Burning Legion invaded through the Broken Isles, distinct class orders organized champions for a common defense.

events.name: The Curse of Ula’tek Reaches the Coiled Isle

date.label: Released August 2026

events.summary: The Midnight campaign continues on the Coiled Isle as Zul’jarra pursues Zul’jan and champions confront the Ula’tek threat.
events.description: Blizzard states that Zul’jan’s actions unleashed Ula’tek and that the Venomous Abyss raid confronts her. This record does not infer later campaign outcomes.

events.name: The Dark Portal Opens

date.label: The opening of the Dark Portal

events.summary: Gul'dan and the corrupted Guardian Medivh completed a gateway between Draenor and Azeroth, allowing the Horde to cross between worlds.

events.name: The Dark Trolls Settle Near the Well

date.label: Beginning around 15,000 years before the Dark Portal

events.summary: A reclusive dark troll people moved toward the center of Kalimdor and made their home near the Well of Eternity.

events.name: Flashback · Era 7 — The date the Annals give

date.label: Third War historical prologue · exact date disputed in the Annals

events.summary: The Annals begin in a village under threat, but their first date creates a problem this telling will not smooth away. The book says the Scourge was rampaging in the middle of the Second War; another historical account places Darrowshire’s fall in the Third War. The Third War frame is used here because the named Scourge war belongs to that later crisis, while the Annals’ wording remains visible as a contradiction in the record. The village is small and rural, its fate more certain than its date.

events.name: The Annals keep a broken date

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: The Annals give the visitor a written account of Darrowshire’s last battle, including the Second War date that cannot be reconciled here with a Scourge attack in the Third War. This telling cites the book as evidence and labels its chronology disputed rather than silently repairing it. The recollection of combat may preserve names and sequence while the date has been miscopied, retconned, or framed differently; the sources consulted do not let us choose among those explanations.

events.name: Carlin and the bound defenders

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: At Light’s Hope Chapel, Carlin remembers the people of the village and asks that the dead defenders be freed from Scourge service. The quest records a group of spirits bound in hostile forms; its objective count belongs to play mechanics, not a census of everyone who lived or died. The modest chapel in the open Plaguelands gives this act a place of witness, while the spirits’ exact appearance and number remain unknown.

events.name: Davil survives Horgus

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: In the quest’s reenacted battle, Davil is to endure until Horgus is slain. The task reverses the fatal pattern recorded in the Annals without pretending that every part of the old account has been repaired. The defender and the Scourge champion meet in a staged scene, not a recovered battle plan. This moment marks the specific loss the quest allows its visitor to prevent in the remembered battle.

events.name: Davil’s last stand

date.label: Third War historical prologue · exact date disputed in the Annals

events.summary: Davil fights Horgus and the Annals say he strikes the Scourge champion down, only to die of his own wounds. Later sources call this defender Davil Lightfire in the quest and Davil Crokford in the book and history summary. The story holds both names together as a textual variant pending client comparison. His later libram is treated as a memorial clue; the search quest does not establish where it rested during the original battle.

events.name: Davil’s libram at Hearthglen

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: The Heroes quest associates Davil Lightfire’s libram with Hearthglen, carrying a trace of the defender into the fortified human town. Its pale stone and red-white Scarlet banners identify Classic Hearthglen without turning it into Stormwind’s blue-and-gold keep. The book is a recovered clue attributed to Davil, not proof of its exact earlier route or of every hand through which it passed.

events.name: Carlin’s extended account

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: Carlin provides the extended account and the accumulated relics pass back to Chromie. The text describes a plan to revisit the battle and correct its consequences, but the quest delegates the historical decision to a time spell rather than explaining its larger metaphysics. This gathered bundle is a narrative device supported by quest order; the exact composition of every piece and the intervention’s limits are not independently established.

events.name: Pamela hears the battle end

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: After the fighting, the quest brings Joseph’s spirit to Pamela, and the child speaks as if her father will come home. The account presents their reunion as the battle’s remembered resolution; the deeper effect of Chromie’s spell on a lasting timeline remains uncertain. Pamela then entrusts the traveler with a key to a chest behind the house. Her small act of welcome closes the chain with an image of homecoming, while the village’s original loss remains part of the record.

events.name: Joseph’s shield at the ruined farm

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: A separate relic leads to Gahrron’s Withering, where the quest locates Joseph Redpath’s broken shield near a ruined farm. Its damage speaks to the village captain’s remembered role, but the object alone cannot tell how or when it was lost. Here the Plaguelands narrow from the fortified town to a leaning barn, broken fence and pallid field: a rural clue, not a complete account of the battle.

events.name: Horgus enters the battle

date.label: Third War historical prologue · exact date disputed in the Annals

events.summary: The account names Horgus the Ravager among the Scourge force that reaches Darrowshire. Captain Joseph Redpath and Davil lead the village’s defense in the story remembered by the later questline. We can show a small settlement meeting an invading force; we cannot recover its exact formation, the number of attackers, or the moment each defender first fell. The landscape is rendered as the fragile home at stake, not as a measured battlefield plan.

events.name: Marduk turns Joseph

date.label: Third War historical prologue · exact date disputed in the Annals

events.summary: After Davil’s fall, the Annals say Marduk the Black corrupts Joseph Redpath. The village captain becomes a danger to the people he led, and the account ends in Darrowshire’s destruction. The secondary history calls Marduk Blackpool. The two forms may reflect a naming variation, but the evidence gathered here does not settle it. Nor can the broad massacre account tell us the position or final moment of every villager.

events.name: The crystal answers the skulls

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: A mystic crystal responds to five skulls associated by the quest with Scourge that took part in the assault. Their collection is a gameplay task, so it cannot be read as a definitive list of every enemy or a complete battle roster. It adds another layer to Chromie’s reconstruction: selected remains, a remembered account, and relics tied to those who fought. The exact mechanism of the crystal is not explained beyond its use in the quest.

events.name: Era 8 — Marlene’s request

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: In the later Classic quest, a wandering spirit named Marlene asks for help finding Pamela. The road begins in the Plaguelands of another age, where the old village no longer stands whole. This is investigation, not the battle itself: every witness and object will be encountered through the quest’s present-day search. The adventurer remains unnamed, and the order of errands records how the game guides that search, not a known calendar.

events.name: The truth Marlene cannot give Pamela

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: Marlene’s account says Pamela died, while Joseph’s fate leads toward the battle’s corrupted captain. Yet she cannot bring herself to tell the child the whole truth. Her silence is a choice in the quest’s present, shaped by the family’s grief; no hidden motive beyond that account is supplied. The village story now has two witnesses at different distances from the event: a child asking, and an aunt carrying an answer she cannot speak.

events.name: The doll among the ruins

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: Pamela appears among the ruined homes, still waiting in the world her family lost. Her doll is missing, and the quest sends the visitor through the broken settlement to recover its scattered parts. The action belongs to the Classic investigation; it does not establish that the doll lay in these exact visible stones or that the child’s spirit understands the history around her. The small object makes a vast catastrophe personal.

events.name: Pamela asks for her family

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: With the doll restored, Pamela’s questions turn toward her parents and the home she remembers. The quest lets the child’s request lead the investigation onward; it does not give the unnamed traveler a private biography or a new place in the Redpath family. We keep the scene quiet: a remembered child, a found keepsake, and an answer that only relatives and the old records can begin to provide.

events.name: A child hidden from the battle

date.label: Third War historical prologue · exact date disputed in the Annals

events.summary: The later quest gives a more intimate memory: Marlene says she hid Pamela when the fighting came. That account sits uneasily beside the Annals’ sweeping language that the village was destroyed and its inhabitants slain. The story keeps the difference open. Marlene’s report explains why Pamela is encountered as a child’s spirit, but neither source offers an independent account of how every resident met their end.

events.name: The captain falls to corruption

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: The second condition cannot be avoided: Joseph must live long enough to become corrupted, and then the visitor must defeat Redpath the Corrupted. Marduk’s role belongs to the Annals’ account; the quest objectives do not show every cause in the reenactment. The story keeps Joseph’s change distinct from Davil’s survival, so the battle’s altered course does not collapse into a claim that no one was lost or that the Scourge never reached Darrowshire.

events.name: The battle is called back

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: Chromie’s spell returns the traveler to a reenactment of Darrowshire’s battle. The scene is explicitly a remembered, playable past, separated from the present-day investigation. Its instructions focus on outcomes: Davil must remain alive until Horgus falls, and Joseph must live long enough to be corrupted before the corrupted captain is defeated. The quest therefore offers a limited correction inside the replay; it does not erase the evidence that the original village was destroyed.

events.name: The skull and the shattered blade

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: The first relic trail turns toward the remembered villains. The quest associates a skull with Horgus and a broken sword with Marduk, leading the search to different places around the Plaguelands. These are clues chosen by a historical investigation, not excavated proof that the objects lay exactly where the illustration places them. The broken weapon gives Marduk a material trace even while the Annals’ version of his name remains unsettled.

events.name: A ring and a historian

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic quest sequence · exact date unknown

events.summary: A wedding ring becomes the clue that turns a family search toward history. The quest brings the object to Chromie, a bronze dragon who has taken the form of a gnome historian in Andorhal. This small ruined town supplies a believable Classic Plaguelands setting, though the quest does not chart the traveler’s road. The ring binds the family question to Chromie’s larger interest in a battle the living can no longer visit directly.

events.name: The Elven Coalition Creates the Dawnwell

date.label: After the Darkwell assault

events.summary: An elven coalition drives back the Devouring Host, Sylvanas helps force Xal’atath to retreat, and the corrupted fount becomes the Dawnwell.
events.description: The restored fount marks a released chapter outcome. The Harbinger’s retreat is not her final defeat.

events.name: Deathwing Shatters the World

date.label: The Cataclysm

events.summary: Deathwing's return caused the Cataclysm, violently reshaping regions across Azeroth and forcing a world-spanning defense.

events.name: The Dragon Isles Awaken

date.label: After the return from the Shadowlands

events.summary: The Dragon Isles awakened, calling the dragonflights home and opening a new expedition into their ancient inheritance.

events.name: A commission from Booty Bay

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Bodley remembers a commission from Gremnik Rizzlesprang, a goblin smuggler-wizard out of Booty Bay. The job was to take Lord Valthalak’s spellbook from Blackrock Spire. Bodley does not know whether Gremnik meant to study it or sell it, and the manual leaves that motive unresolved. The distinction matters: the company’s contract is documented, but its patron’s private purpose is not.

events.name: A plea that cannot wait

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Anthion’s request carries two losses at once. He has already died in the attempt, yet the thought of losing Ysida still binds him to the road. The quest asks for a living woman held by the Baron, not for a heroic last stand by her husband. No timer is needed in the telling: the source gives the plea and the danger, while the hourglass belongs to the dungeon challenge rather than to a new historical event.

events.name: Alternative fate · Isalien

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Isalien left the company for a pilgrimage to Dire Maul, seeking answers about her night elf heritage and perhaps the magic within her amulet piece. Bodley remembers her as a friend of Falrin. In the city’s old kaldorei halls, she was ambushed by Alzzin the Wildshaper and his forces. The manual leaves her at another haunted place: a former companion drawn toward knowledge, then overtaken by the same scattered curse.

events.name: Alternative fate · Jarien and Sothos

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Jarien and Sothos, siblings of the Veiled Blade, turned toward the Scarlet Crusade after the company dissolved. They sought knighthood at Stratholme. Bodley’s account says Sothos failed the final trial; Jarien defended her brother and demanded that they be admitted together. Grand Crusader Dathrohan killed them both. The amulet piece they carried further twisted their spirits. Their chapter, too, is one possible haunted locus in the family of routes.

events.name: Alternative fate · Kormok

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Another branch follows Kormok to Scholomance. Once a member of the Veiled Blade, the two-headed ogre became drawn to necromancy; the manual describes one head as clever and cold, the other more foolish. After the company broke apart, he sought further study at Scholomance. Valthalak’s spectral assassins reached him there and killed him before Ras Frostwhisper. The record remembers a comrade turned toward dangerous art, then found by the curse.

events.name: Alternative fate · Mor Grayhoof

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: One remembered branch leads to Mor Grayhoof. He survived the fall into Lower Blackrock Spire, but trolls captured him and War Master Voone tortured him. The spectral assassins finished what the fall had not. Mor’s story is one of the manual’s haunted loci; it is an alternative account of a former companion’s fate, not an assertion that every adventurer fought every spirit in this order.

events.name: Bodley, unseen on the balcony

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Near the entrance balcony of Blackrock Spire, Bodley appears only to one who can see ghosts. He had gone back toward the fortress and never returned. The quest giver fears he is dead; Bodley confirms it without ceremony and asks for help undoing the company’s wrong. If the top piece is already found, he can point toward the other two. His greeting is warm, even here, where the old danger began.

events.name: Falrin remembers an old friend

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: In Dire Maul’s Athenaeum, Anthion’s old friend Falrin Treeshaper listens to the request. He had thought Anthion dead. Falrin agrees to help prepare an enchantment that can draw Theldren into a fight; his anger at the ogres is personal, rooted in the death of his brother. The required collection is a task in play, not a separate historical episode. What matters to the story is that an old bond supplies the means for a dangerous meeting.

events.name: Ysida in the Slaughter House

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: The way leads through Stratholme to its Slaughter House, where Rivendare holds Ysida. The walls are steeped in the Scourge’s greenish corruption, but the quest’s purpose is rescue: reach her alive and bring her beyond the Baron’s reach. The art marks the room as an interpretation of the Classic dungeon, not a measured reconstruction. Ysida has endured the city’s horror; the next journey carries a message toward the husband she believes is lost.

events.name: Mea Culpa, Lord Valthalak

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: In the Beast’s chamber, the brazier calls Valthalak back into a body that can be confronted. After the battle, the restored amulet is used on his corpse and his spirit appears, whole again. He recognizes that the seeker was not among the original thieves and demands his property back. The quest does not give the mortal a new claim to the medallion; it asks the traveler to return it to its owner and carry his answer back to Bodley.

events.name: Anthion’s parting words

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: With the top piece returned, Anthion explains the danger that he could not see before. The Veiled Blade split Valthalak’s amulet into three parts out of greed, not knowing that it held much of the warlock’s soul. The curse followed. Anthion asks the seeker to find Bodley, who can guide the search for the other pieces. At last, Anthion believes he may rest; his part in the company’s wrong has become a plea to set it right.

events.name: Proof of life

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Ysida gives the rescuer her locket to carry back to Anthion. She believes he perished while trying to save her, and the token is her proof that she remains alive. When the message reaches the roadside ghost, Anthion learns that the rescue succeeded. Their reunion is brief and divided by death, yet Ysida’s survival releases him from the fear that held him there. He can now offer help in the work that remains.

events.name: Safe for now

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Valthalak tells the traveler to return to the Veiled Blade and say they are safe—for now. Bodley is astonished that the spirit will call off his assassins, though the promise carries a warning of future harm. The manual still speaks of echoes at the haunted loci, and the company itself has not been restored. Its members remain scattered among separate lives and deaths. What is repaired is the amulet, and for this moment, the pursuit it unleashed.

events.name: The brazier is prepared

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Bodley prepares a brazier able to call the spirit from its old lair. The chain asks for specific components, but their collection is not another history of the company. Its purpose is to attune the brazier and make the final encounter possible. The manual names haunted places to give the wider meaning: Valthalak’s power has marked the places where his former companions fell, and the Beast’s chamber remains the last of those sites.

events.name: The company flees the risen spirit

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Valthalak rose as a spirit and called spectral assassins against the mercenaries. Their struggle also roused defenders in the Spire. Most of the Veiled Blade escaped, but safety proved brief: the assassins pursued them wherever they hid. The company soon broke apart, its quarrel made worse by a curse that followed each shard. In the confusion Mor Grayhoof fell toward the lower reaches of the fortress, where his own path would end.

events.name: A fragment taken by Theldren

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Anthion’s next account turns from rescue to the Veiled Blade’s spoils. The company did not understand the medallion’s importance, so it was divided with their other plunder. A dwarf named Theldren took the first piece. Anthion tried to win it back and was beaten badly; the fragment would have to be claimed through another challenge. The amulet is already more than an ornament, though its danger has not yet been named.

events.name: The former general of the Spire

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Before Drakkisath, Lord Valthalak was a drakonid noble and warlock who had served as Blackrock Spire’s general. The Veiled Blade entered the upper fortress, slew him, and took the spellbook. Bodley recalls that the company knew too little of Valthalak’s power over souls to understand what they had disturbed. The lair is now called the Beast’s chamber. The manual’s account makes clear that the company’s successful contract was the beginning of its ruin.

events.name: The ghost at Stratholme’s gate

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: At the Eastern Plaguelands road, a goblin device lets the living hear Anthion Harmon. Death has not quieted his concern: Ysida, his wife, was captured by Baron Rivendare inside Stratholme. Anthion says he tried to reach her and failed. He asks the seeker to finish the rescue. The city rises behind him through bare branches and grey-green haze; within it, the question is simple and terrible—whether Ysida still lives.

events.name: The medallion in Kormok’s hands

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: When the company prepared to leave with the book, Kormok claimed Valthalak’s amulet as his share. His insistence turned the group against itself. They argued, nearly came to blows, and finally broke the medallion into three pieces. Only later did they learn that it housed much of Valthalak’s spirit. The distribution followed a lot; Theldren’s top fragment had already returned through Anthion’s challenge, while the other pieces scattered among former companions.

events.name: Finding the other two pieces

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Bodley guides the search to two further pieces. The quest versions can direct a class or faction branch toward one of several haunted companions; they are alternate targets from the same company history. The four accounts just heard are arranged here as memorials, not as four mandatory kills by one canonical traveler. When the missing pieces are brought together with Theldren’s top fragment, the medallion can be made whole again.

events.name: The Challenge in Blackrock Depths

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Beneath Blackrock Mountain, the Ring of Law becomes the stage for the challenge. As High Justice Grimstone sentences the intruders, they plant Falrin’s banner. Theldren cannot resist the provocation; he enters the arena with his gladiators. The team composition can vary, so this scene gives no fixed roster or race to the company. The battle retrieves the top piece and changes the next question: now the remaining fragments must be traced to Anthion’s other companions.

events.name: Two doors into the same story

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Dungeon Set 2 questline

events.summary: Deliana speaks from Ironforge; Mokvar speaks from Orgrimmar. Their faction quests are separate doors into the same old wound, not a shared meeting or a single adventurer’s simultaneous allegiance. Each directs a seeker toward Anthion Harmon, whose ghost waits beyond Stratholme. The armor work that frames the journey is only its threshold. Ahead lie a rescue, a company’s last contract, and a medallion whose pieces carried more than any of its owners understood.

events.name: The Dwarven Succession Crisis Opens

date.label: Approximately 230 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: The death of Ironforge's high king broke a tense balance among the Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, and Dark Iron clans and opened a war for the mountain city.

events.name: The Early Troll Powers Rise

date.label: About 16,000 years before the Dark Portal

events.summary: Troll peoples flourished across the forests and jungles of ordered Kalimdor, with the Zandalar, Amani, Gurubashi, and Drakkari among the powers that took shape.

events.name: Azsharite for the weapon

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: A name alone cannot break Razelikh’s hold. The chain next calls for azsharite, a material gathered in Azshara and brought into the weapon-making task. The quest’s collection condition is not retold as a count or a single dramatic excavation. What changes is the preparation: the hunt has found its target, and the seeker now carries material chosen for the Felbane armament that will make the final confrontation possible.

events.name: Bengor brings the lost orders

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: In the Horde telling, Bengor is found wounded in the Swamp of Sorrows. He reports that the dispatch was ambushed and the Warchief’s orders lost. His testimony brings the seeker to Trebor and gives the campaign a practical beginning: before the old soldier can speak of his shame, the missing command must be recovered. The chain does not turn the Alliance introduction into the same journey; it offers another way to reach the shared wound.

events.name: Felbane takes shape

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: At Galvan’s camp in inland Stranglethorn, the material becomes Felbane weaponry. The green canopy, hanging vines and warm air make the setting recognizably different from Azshara’s coast; this is no harbor scene at Booty Bay. Galvan’s part is the transformation of gathered material into a prepared weapon. The records support the chain’s order and purpose, while the exact craft process and selectable weapon form remain matters for comparison with the Classic client.

events.name: A sign of hope, and an unfinished charge

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The final quest records Razelikh’s defeat and asks that his horn be returned to Trebor as a sign of hope. It also asks for the Ward of the Defiler so Trebor can destroy it. The request is clear; the destruction itself is not shown as a completed event in the evidence used here. Trebor’s story reaches a hard-won answer for the bound souls and the demon who held them. It does not record the fall of the Burning Legion, or every fate within its reach.

events.name: Kirith at Serpent’s Coil

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The quest turns toward Serpent’s Coil, where Kirith the Damned bars the way. The setting changes from open badlands to a low cave mouth on the coast. There the adventurer defeats the demon and the chain yields a new account through Kirith’s spirit. The art presents the beast in a broad, readable silhouette; it is not a reconstruction of the cave’s exact layout or proof of details absent from the quest record.

events.name: The amulet has three pieces

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Kirith’s spirit explains the next obstacle: Razelikh cannot be reached until the shattered amulet is made whole. Its three pieces are held by the demon’s lieutenants. The quest dialogue supplies the clue, not a new claim about Kirith’s final fate. The fragments now give the scattered work a shape. Trebor’s grievance can be answered only by confronting the power behind the bindings, and the seeker needs both knowledge and a weapon for that meeting.

events.name: Loramus and the demon hunter’s counsel

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The chain reaches Loramus Thalipedes on Azshara’s cold eastern shore. In the Classic quest account, the demon hunter helps direct the work that lies ahead: learn the demon’s true name and prepare a means to challenge him. The coast is broad and wind-cut, a different world from the Blasted Lands’ dry scar. This telling uses Loramus’s Classic-era counsel only; later retellings of his story do not replace what this quest chain records.

events.name: The name behind the title

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The search crosses Azshara’s pale coastal ruins, where the quest steps call for Hetaera’s blood and seek Lord Arkkoroc’s knowledge. The demon known as Razelikh the Defiler bears a truer name: Rakh’likh. That distinction is the chain’s discovery. Here, the old temple stone and blue water frame a hunt for usable knowledge, not a claim that every step took place in one room or followed an exact route along the coast.

events.name: Return with the forged weapons

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The quest line turns back to Trebor with the weapon prepared and the amulet’s scattered fragments to unite. This is an editorial journey through quest destinations, not a drawn route: its tasks name the regions but do not document each road taken. The exposed Blasted Lands return as the place where old bonds and new preparations converge. The demon’s title, the weapon and the amulet are now part of one effort to reach the Rise.

events.name: The stones that bind them

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The quest objective names eighteen bound servants: nine held by Razelikh and three each by Sevine, Allistarj and Grol. Their binding is represented by stones spread across the region, with no exact placement claimed here. The quest asks the seeker to break the hold upon them. In the exposed red earth, Trebor’s old loss becomes more than a memory: it becomes a task that can still release those who suffered under his command.

events.name: At the Rise of the Defiler

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: At the Rise of the Defiler, the united amulet lets the seeker bring the demon into the final contest. The known title falls away before the true name: Razelikh is Rakh’likh. Trebor’s old appeal has led here, from the souls once bound by the demon’s servants to a challenge against their master. The quests frame the meeting as a dangerous group confrontation but give no fixed battle formation. At the Rise, every preparation finds its purpose against the master whose servants once held Trebor’s soldiers.

events.name: The spirits may rest

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: When the binding stones are broken, the completion text says the tortured souls can rest. It gives Trebor the mercy he had sought for his soldiers, though the count remains unsettled by the separate nineteen-men line. The story pauses over that release without supplying names for the dead or turning each stone into a separate battle. A long burden has eased; the power behind the chains still stands.

events.name: Three lieutenants, three fragments

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The remaining amulet pieces come from Razelikh’s lieutenants: Allistarj, Sevine and Grol. Their encounters are separate, not one gathering in a field. In the tour they form a deliberate triptych, a memorial arrangement of three independent confrontations. When the fragments are brought together, the amulet is whole. Its completion opens the way that Kirith described, though the precise order of lieutenant encounters is not treated as a historical sequence beyond the quest dependency.

events.name: Trebor’s tale of sorrow

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Trebor recounts failure in battle, then a return to the Blasted Lands to rescue the men left behind. The account is one of defeat and obligation: he could not leave the captured soldiers to their torment. The reproduced Horde dialogue speaks of nineteen of his men, while the binding-stone objective counts eighteen bound servants. These are kept as two source details in tension. The surviving evidence does not resolve the difference.

events.name: Two roads to the Fallen Hero

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Fallen Hero quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The Blasted Lands are a country of exposed earth and old ruin, where Trebor’s defeat still has living consequences. Classic gives his story two introductions. The Alliance quest approaches him through a plea for common action against the Legion; the Horde chain follows lost orders and a courier’s report. These are separate faction paths, not one traveler’s shared itinerary. They meet at Trebor, whose concern has outlasted his own life: the soldiers he could not save.

events.name: The First War Begins

date.label: After the Dark Portal opens

events.summary: Horde forces entered Azeroth and began the war against the Kingdom of Stormwind.

events.name: The Forsaken Emerge in Lordaeron

date.label: As the Lich King's control weakens after the Legion's defeat

events.summary: Sylvanas and other undead broke from the Lich King's control and established a new, precarious power in the ruins of Lordaeron.

events.name: The Fourth War Campaign Ends

date.label: At the close of the Fourth War campaign

events.summary: A rebellion joined with Alliance pressure against Sylvanas's rule, bringing the war campaign to its end without erasing its losses.

events.name: The Fourth War Erupts

date.label: After the Legion campaign

events.summary: Alliance and Horde entered a global war of footholds, reprisals, and deepening fractures after the Legion's defeat.

events.name: The Great Sundering

date.label: c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal

events.summary: The Well's destruction tore primordial Kalimdor apart, drowned great reaches of land, and left the Maelstrom at the center of a new ocean.

events.name: Grom Breaks Mannoroth's Bond

date.label: During the Kalimdor campaign

events.summary: After falling again beneath Mannoroth's corruption, Grom joined Thrall against the pit lord and died in the act that broke the immediate demonic bond over their people.

events.name: Gul'dan Abandons the Second War

date.label: During the Horde's northern campaign

events.summary: Gul'dan withdrew forces from the Horde's campaign for his own expedition, weakening Orgrim's offensive at a critical time.

events.name: Gul'dan Forms the Shadow Council

date.label: During the political consolidation of the clans

events.summary: After Ner'zhul resisted the Legion's course, Gul'dan organized a concealed warlock council and tightened hidden control around the forming Horde.

events.name: The Highborne Are Exiled

date.label: Approximately 7,300 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Conflict over arcane practice ended with a Highborne population leaving Kalimdor under Dath'Remar's leadership.

events.name: The Highborne Open the Way

date.label: At the opening of the War of the Ancients

events.summary: Azshara's favored Highborne used the Well to establish a portal through which the Burning Legion could enter Azeroth.

events.name: The Horde Is Defeated and the Dark Portal Is Destroyed

date.label: At the end of the Second War; working chronology

events.summary: The Alliance drove the Horde back to the gateway, destroyed the original Dark Portal, and captured many of the defeated orcs.

events.name: The Defenders of Hyjal Unite

date.label: Before Archimonde reaches Nordrassil

events.summary: Night elves, the New Horde, and Alliance survivors accepted a temporary common defense as the Legion advanced toward Mount Hyjal.

events.name: Illidan Assaults the Frozen Throne

date.label: After Kil'jaeden commands Illidan to destroy the Frozen Throne

events.summary: Illidan returned from Outland and drove toward Icecrown, but Arthas defeated him before reaching the Frozen Throne.

events.name: Illidan Creates a Second Well

date.label: In the immediate aftermath of the Sundering

events.summary: Illidan used preserved water from the original Well to create a new arcane well upon Mount Hyjal and was imprisoned after the act was discovered.

events.name: Illidan Seizes Power in Outland

date.label: After the Battle of Mount Hyjal

events.summary: Illidan and his allies closed portals, defeated Magtheridon's rule, and established a new center of power in Outland.

events.name: The Iron Horde Opens an Alternate Front

date.label: After the Siege of Orgrimmar

events.summary: An invasion from an alternate Draenor opened a separate-world campaign against the Iron Horde.

events.name: The Kaldorei Ascend

date.label: Across generations beside the Well

events.summary: Changed by long proximity to the Well, the emerging kaldorei mastered arcane power, built cities, and expanded across Kalimdor.

events.name: A key in three pieces

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Khadgar explains that, while stranded in Outland, he split his key into three and hid the pieces inside enchanted containers. The places seemed safe when he chose them; Outland has changed since then. His explanation gives the search its shape, but not a single road: each fragment lies in a separate dungeon, and each location reflects a world now fought over by new powers.

events.name: Beneath the sealed tower

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Alturus gives the seeker a Violet Scrying Crystal and asks for readings from underground water in the Master’s Cellar. In the quest’s report, the expected arcane currents are absent: the tower registers as a vast energy vacuum, with only a faint demonic echo. That phrase is Alturus’s reading of the crystal, not a confirmed identity for the presence. The cellar returns a warning, but not yet an answer.

events.name: A question among the ashes

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: After studying the journal, Alturus proposes that Medivh may have woven some of his essence into the magic that defeated Arcanagos. If so, he reasons, a trace might remain in the dragon’s bones. The quest sends the seeker to find a Charred Bone Fragment in the mountains south of Karazhan. This is Alturus’s hypothesis and a search for evidence, not a confirmation that the essence can be recovered.

events.name: A report reaches Dalaran

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Alturus sends his report to Archmage Cedric in Dalaran’s old crater. Cedric has learned that the tower sealed itself off and that the Violet Eye lost contact with agents within it. The new reading gives the old silence another urgency. Cedric points toward one person who might reopen the way: Khadgar, Medivh’s former apprentice, now living in Shattrath. The ruined crater is Dalaran’s original site, not the city’s later home in Northrend.

events.name: The first fragment in Auchindoun

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The first fragment rests in the Shadow Labyrinth, among passages occupied by the Shadow Council. Khadgar’s account places the container there because the labyrinth once seemed a safe hiding place. The return of the fragment changes the key from a distant memory into a recoverable object. It does not yet open the tower; two pieces remain beyond reach.

events.name: Kalynna’s offer

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Alturus sends the bone to Kalynna Lathred in Area 52. She once belonged to the Kirin Tor, but now follows studies her old order forbade. The fragment’s essence, Alturus says, is lifeless—like Arcanagos. Kalynna believes she can help, but her own research has a cost. Her answer turns the Violet Eye’s question into a bargain between scholars with different boundaries.

events.name: Two books, two halls

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Kalynna asks for two books before she will complete the favor. The Tome of Dusk belongs to the orc warlock Nethekurse in the Shattered Halls; the Book of Forgotten Names is held by Darkweaver Syth in Sethekk Halls. The quest requires heroic versions of both dungeons. These are the terms of a research exchange, not separate historical turning points, and the two halls retain their distinct landscapes in this paired itinerary.

events.name: Khadgar in Shattrath

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: In Shattrath, Khadgar receives Alturus’s account and sees a familiar problem in it. Karazhan cannot simply be forced open; the Master’s Key once held that power, and he knows the key’s history. He will help restore it, though the next stages will cross Outland’s changed strongholds. The meeting begins the fragment quest line. It is a new undertaking prompted by Alturus’s report, not proof that the Violet Eye has already learned what happened inside the tower.

events.name: A memory of Arcanagos

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: On the Master’s Terrace, the journal opens onto an older meeting. The blue dragon Arcanagos warns Medivh that a dark power seeks to use him, and urges him to leave the tower. Medivh refuses. Magic burns through the dragon from within; Arcanagos flies away aflame. The scene is a memory carried by the journal, not a new event occurring during the Violet Eye’s present investigation.

events.name: Nightbane on the terrace

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: With Kalynna’s materials placed in a Blackened Urn, the seeker returns to the Master’s Terrace and sets it alight. The quest says the released energy raises Arcanagos’s charred remains as Nightbane. The adventurer defeats the dragon and carries its essence back to Alturus, whose hope is to study what the fragment may reveal about Medivh. The chain ends with a sample and a research question—not a complete explanation of the Guardian’s magic, nor a later chapter in Arcanagos’s history.

events.name: Reports from Deadwind Pass

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Archmage Alturus watches the road below Karazhan while the Violet Eye studies a tower that has kept its doors closed. His first assignments open along two parallel paths: Arcane Disturbances and Restless Activity. One sends the seeker beneath the tower; the other concerns the restless dead around it. The quests establish a troubled place and an order to investigate. They do not establish that either task caused the tower’s condition, or that the source of every disturbance is already known.

events.name: The key returns to Shattrath

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The restored key returns to Khadgar in Shattrath, and the attunement chain reaches its stated end. A way into Karazhan now exists. The tower’s condition and the fate of its trapped investigators remain matters for the Violet Eye to examine. That distinction closes one quest and leaves another question standing at the gate.

events.name: A fragment under the Steamvault

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The second container is found in the Steamvault beneath Coilfang Reservoir. Khadgar recalls hiding it under Serpent Lake before the place was known by that name; he suspects the naga’s great drain carried it into the reservoir. That explanation is his best account of a changed landscape, not a witnessed transfer. The fragment is recovered, while the precise course of its movement remains uncertain.

events.name: A separate search for the journal

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The Violet Eye’s next inquiry is related by the tower, not by a shared quest dependency: after establishing a foothold inside Karazhan and earning the required standing, Alturus asks the adventurer to find Medivh’s Journal. Agents sent before have not returned; Wravien was the last named seeker. This is a distinct research chain joined here for its evidence about the tower’s history. It does not follow automatically from handing Khadgar the key.

events.name: The investigators among the books

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Inside the Guardian’s Library, Wravien struggles to remember his commission and sends the seeker to Gradav. Gradav also cannot leave his own work, then points toward Kamsis. The three exchanges make the library’s abundance part of the obstacle: each agent offers a fragment of direction, while none can simply lead the search to its end. Their quest dialogue records confusion and fixation; it does not fully explain what the tower has done to them.

events.name: The Master’s Touch

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Khadgar restores the key but says it will remain useless without Medivh’s consent. In the Black Morass, the seeker travels to a remembered past at the Opening of the Dark Portal. There, Medivh recognizes the key as Khadgar’s and acknowledges that he has not yet given it to his apprentice. The meeting belongs to a time-travel quest scene, not to a present-day journey through the swamp. The key receives the permission Khadgar could not grant for himself.

events.name: The Shade of Aran and the journal

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Kamsis directs the search toward the Shade of Aran, Medivh’s father. When the shade is overcome, Medivh’s Journal is recovered from the encounter and returned to the Violet Eye’s inquiry. The discovery changes the work from searching for a lost book to reading what the book can reveal. Its pages are not a neutral report from an observer: the next quest treats them as a way to witness one of Medivh’s own memories.

events.name: The prison above Netherstorm

date.label: The Burning Crusade · original quest chronology; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The third fragment lies within the Arcatraz, a prison in the Tempest Keep complex. Khadgar had hidden it while the naaru held the fortress; by the time the seeker arrives, Kael’thas’s forces have turned the vessel into a place of confinement. The key’s last piece is retrieved from a refuge that has become dangerous. The three fragments can now be taken back to their maker.

events.name: The Dimensius Crisis on K’aresh

date.label: During Ghosts of K’aresh (2025)

events.summary: The struggle over the Dark Heart reaches shattered K’aresh, where the Shadow Guard seeks to restore Dimensius.
events.description: This offworld campaign is presented as a separate worldspace. The source links the Dimensius crisis to the next Worldsoul Saga chapter; the atlas does not assign it an Azeroth map position.

events.name: Kil'jaeden Finds the Draenei on Draenor

date.label: Approximately thirteen years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Kil'jaeden discovered Velen's exiles on Draenor and chose the orc clans as the instrument of his revenge.

events.name: The Burning Legion Enters Azeroth

date.label: After the Highborne portal opened

events.summary: Demonic forces poured through the portal at Zin-Azshari and began destroying the empire whose court had admitted them.

events.name: Lei Shen Unites the Mogu

date.label: During the age of divided southern kingdoms

events.summary: Lei Shen overcame rival mogu kings and gathered their competing realms into a single imperial power.

events.name: The Lich King Falls at Icecrown

date.label: During the Northrend campaign

events.summary: The campaign through Northrend reached Icecrown, where Arthas's reign as the Lich King ended.

events.name: The Long Vigil Begins

date.label: After Nordrassil was established

events.summary: Post-Sundering kaldorei society took up a long watch over Kalimdor and against the return of the Burning Legion.

events.name: Lordaeron Falls to the Scourge

date.label: After Arthas returns from Northrend

events.summary: Arthas returned as a death knight, killed his father, and helped bring the kingdom of Lordaeron under the Scourge.

events.name: Anduin Lothar Falls Near Blackrock Spire

date.label: During the Alliance counteroffensive in the Second War

events.summary: Lothar died during the confrontation near Blackrock Spire, creating a moment of shock that Turalyon turned into resolve.

events.name: The Void Assault on Quel’Thalas

date.label: At the opening of Midnight (March 2026)

events.summary: Xal’atath and the Devouring Host assault the Sunwell; Quel’Thalas survives the first incursion after defenders force a temporary retreat.
events.description: The first defense buys time while Lightbloom and other pressures continue to threaten the homeland.

events.name: The Mogu Empire Expands

date.label: After Lei Shen's unification

events.summary: The new empire subdued neighboring peoples and imposed its rule across much of the southern lands later known as Pandaria.

events.name: Neltharion Turns the Dragon Soul on His Allies

date.label: During the War of the Ancients

events.summary: After using the Dragon Soul against the Legion, Neltharion revealed his betrayal and shattered the unity of the dragonflights.

events.name: Ner'zhul Is Deceived Against the Draenei

date.label: Before Gul'dan assumes the Legion's work

events.summary: Kil'jaeden exploited Ner'zhul's authority and grief to turn orc suspicion and violence toward the draenei.

events.name: The New Horde Crosses to Kalimdor

date.label: As the northern crisis widens
