events.summary: Warned of the coming danger, Thrall led the New Horde west across the sea and began building a future in Kalimdor.

events.name: Resistance Forms Against the Invasion

date.label: As the Legion spread beyond Zin-Azshari

events.summary: Kaldorei who rejected Azshara's course organized a resistance in which Malfurion, Tyrande, and Illidan each played consequential roles.

events.name: Nordrassil Is Planted

date.label: After the second Well was discovered

events.summary: A World Tree was planted over the new Well at Hyjal, binding the postwar refuge to a new charge of protection.

events.name: The Assault of N'Zoth Is Defeated

date.label: At the end of the N'Zoth campaign

events.summary: Champions carried the struggle into Ny'alotha and ended N'Zoth's immediate assault on Azeroth.

events.name: N'Zoth Is Unleashed

date.label: After the Fourth War campaign

events.summary: N'Zoth's release brought assaults and corrupting visions against an already wounded Azeroth.

events.name: Arrival of the Old Gods

date.label: After untold ages of elemental conflict

events.summary: A group of Old Gods struck Azeroth from the Great Dark, embedded themselves in different parts of the world, and extended their influence toward its core.

events.name: The Old Gods Are Contained

date.label: After the fall of the Black Empire

events.summary: Unable to remove the remaining Old Gods without repeating the wound caused by Y'Shaarj's destruction, the keepers bound them in prisons beneath Azeroth.

events.name: Scattering of the Old Gods

date.label: Before the Old Gods struck Azeroth

events.summary: The Void Lords made the Old Gods and cast them through the Great Dark, hoping that some would find and corrupt a world-soul.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label. The cosmography asserts sequence and purpose but no origin coordinate, route, or measurable number of Old Gods.

events.name: Blood and the Drakefire Amulet

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: In Upper Blackrock Spire, the adventurers face General Drakkisath and bring his blood to Haleh. From that trial comes the Drakefire Amulet, a ward that allows its bearer to withstand Onyxia’s lair. The Alliance has gone from suspicion to exposure and now to preparation. The key is won; the descent into the dragon’s den waits ahead.

events.name: A final skull over the Wetlands

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Axtroz waits amid the windswept Wetlands, where rain and low cloud soften the coast. This final dragon trial completes the tribute demanded by Emberstrife. Across Kalimdor’s distant shores and the Eastern Kingdoms, each challenge has brought the adventurers nearer to the mountain. Now their road turns back to Blackrock, where Drakkisath waits.

events.name: Finding Rexxar

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Across Desolace, the adventurers seek Rexxar, a wandering champion of the Horde. His place between the wilds and settled life makes him the guide to a difficult next task. Here the great campaign narrows to a search for one champion moving through an immense, sparse land. Rexxar sets the terms for learning how an adventurer might pass the protections around Onyxia’s lair.

events.name: A shadow over the Burning Steppes

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: In the Burning Steppes, black dragonkin gather beneath a sky troubled by ash. Their attacks turn a frontier alarm into a question about the reach of the black dragonflight. The Alliance investigation begins with scattered signs and grows toward the mountain that shelters them. The evidence points to a danger with a foothold beyond the wilds; it does not yet reveal the hand guiding Stormwind’s court.

events.name: A path to Haleh

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: From the capital, the road winds into blue-white winter and brings the adventurers to Haleh. The Dragon’s Eye is the token that opens her counsel, turning Stormwind’s revelation into preparation. She names the test that lies ahead: the blood of a mighty black dragon, taken high within Blackrock Spire. Frost will soon give way to furnace heat.

events.name: The elder’s counsel

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: At Orgrimmar, Eitrigg’s counsel turns the reports into a charge for the Horde. The old veteran understands the danger gathering around Blackrock and sends the adventurers back toward the stronghold with a clearer purpose. The city’s red stone and timber frame a different kind of authority from Stormwind’s court: experience offered in service to the Horde. Its path leads next to a contest for Blackrock Spire.

events.name: The dragon who tests the mask

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: In the heat and dark water of Dustwallow Marsh, Emberstrife tests the forged appearance and sends the adventurers to claim dragon skulls from distant guardians. Three trials await beneath different skies, where the black dragonflight and its rivals still shape the wilds. Emberstrife will accept each skull as part of his demand; Myranda’s borrowed shape must hold until the passage is won.

events.name: A challenge in Blackrock Spire

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: The Horde’s orders bring the adventurers against Warchief Rend Blackhand in Blackrock Spire. His defeat and the proof carried away from it fulfill the charge entrusted to them. The mountain holds more than one danger, and the struggle with Rend belongs to the Horde’s own contest of power. It is a separate road from Windsor’s rescue, even as both paths approach the black dragon’s shadow.

events.name: The Great Masquerade

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Before the assembled court, Katrana Prestor’s disguise falls away. The woman who had stood near Stormwind’s seat of power is revealed as Onyxia, the black dragon whose agents troubled the frontier. Dragonkin answer her presence, and Bolvar stands against the assault as the adventurers fight to defend the Keep. The conspiracy is exposed, yet Onyxia escapes the city. Stormwind has found its hidden enemy, not ended the danger.

events.name: The blood of Drakkisath

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: The Horde returns to Upper Blackrock Spire to confront General Drakkisath. The blood taken from this powerful black dragon completes the trial Rexxar laid before them. The Alliance has passed through its own hands to reach Haleh; the Horde has followed its leaders and its own road. Their stories share a threshold, but each company bears a separate history.

events.name: The way out of the mountain

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: The escape from Blackrock Depths is hard won. Windsor leads the way through hostile halls while his rescuers hold open each turn in the passage. Stormwind cannot hear its witness while he remains beneath the mountain. When the group emerges, the marshal can return to the city and place what he knows before the people who must judge it.

events.name: Into the dragon’s lair

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: The Drakefire Amulet opens the way to Onyxia’s Lair, where a band of champions at last faces the black dragon herself. The road began differently for those who came from Stormwind and those who answered the Horde’s call; each company enters beneath its own banners. Fire shivers across the stone as Onyxia takes wing. The struggle reaches its summit in this original Classic account, though its nameless adventurers are remembered as a company, not a single chosen champion.

events.name: Rexxar’s Drakefire Amulet

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Back with Rexxar, the adventurers receive the Drakefire Amulet. The token bears the protection gathered from every trial and opens the way before them. The Horde has come to this gate by a road all its own: through intelligence, Eitrigg’s counsel, Thrall’s word, Rexxar’s charge and a dragon’s blood. At the mountain’s foot, that labor gives way to a final descent.

events.name: A shred of evidence

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: A crumpled note points toward the fragments Windsor needs. The search passes through the forge and deeper chambers of Blackrock Mountain, where small pieces of a document matter more than the strength of the gates. Recovered evidence gives Windsor grounds to leave his cell and face the city again. This is the work of a rescue and an investigation together: one carries the other back into the light.

events.name: The marshal returns

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Windsor comes back to Stormwind with the evidence gathered in Blackrock. The capital that once seemed distant from the frontier danger now becomes the stage for its reckoning. Bolvar receives the marshal’s return, and the city’s uneasy court gathers around the claim. The journey has changed the question: instead of asking whether the marshal can escape, the Alliance must decide whether it can hear him.

events.name: Myranda’s borrowed shape

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Rexxar’s instruction leads to Myranda the Hag in the blighted Western Plaguelands. Her magic prepares a means of taking a dragon’s shape, a disguise needed for the work to come. It does not make the adventurers dragons or erase their purpose; it is a temporary tool for passing the watchers of the mountain. In the scarred land, the Horde’s road turns from finding an ally to testing a dangerous deception.

events.name: Three trials, three horizons

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Three guardians stand in lands far apart: Chronalis beneath the Tanaris sun, Scryer amid Winterspring snow, and Somnus beneath the Swamp of Sorrows’ green canopy. Each place holds its own weather and color, and each dragon bears one part of the trial Emberstrife set. With the three skulls gathered, the Horde can complete his charge and carry Myranda’s borrowed shape toward the black dragon’s mountain.

events.name: The court’s new voice

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Reports from Redridge and the Burning Steppes carry the search into Stormwind. In the Keep, Bolvar Fordragon bears the kingdom’s regency while Countess Katrana Prestor speaks with unusual influence. To the investigators, the mystery is no longer only a nest of dragonkin: a trusted figure sits within the very hall they are trying to protect. The resemblance between rumor and conspiracy remains a question still to be proved.

events.name: Orders from the Badlands

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Far from Stormwind’s court, the Horde receives a separate summons in the Badlands. Orders point toward the stronghold of Blackrock Spire and the power held there. This path does not begin as an answer to Windsor’s investigation; it grows from Horde intelligence, leaders and obligations of its own. The same mountain appears on another horizon, where a different people must decide what its threat means.

events.name: Thrall’s account

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: At Orgrimmar, Thrall speaks of the danger and sends the search outward toward Rexxar. The Warchief’s words widen the matter into a concern for the Horde itself. The tale now leaves the city’s red stone and timber for the open country. Ahead lies a champion whose life at the edge of society has made him known across Kalimdor.

events.name: The marshal in Blackrock Depths

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Onyxia story before the Wrath raid rerelease

events.summary: Deep in Blackrock Depths, Marshal Windsor has been held away from the court whose danger he understands. His account is not enough by itself to undo the power that silenced him. The adventurers find a soldier who has carried the truth through imprisonment, and a trail of evidence scattered through the fortress. The mountain’s iron rooms have become the place where a political mystery waits for its missing proof.

events.name: Orc Clans Drink Mannoroth's Blood

date.label: Before the final assault on Shattrath

events.summary: Many orc leaders accepted Mannoroth's blood and its power, binding the Horde more deeply to the Legion; Durotan kept the Frostwolves from drinking.

events.name: Orgrim Doomhammer Becomes Warchief

date.label: During the First War

events.summary: Orgrim killed Blackhand, broke much of the Shadow Council's concealed power, and assumed leadership of the Horde.

events.name: The Dark Portal Leads Back to Outland

date.label: After the Ahn'Qiraj campaign

events.summary: A renewed passage through the Dark Portal carried Azeroth's forces into shattered Outland and the conflicts rooted there.

events.name: The Pandaren Revolution

date.label: After generations of mogu rule

events.summary: Resistance associated with Kang spread among the mogu's subject peoples until the imperial order broke and the southern lands entered a new age.

events.name: Pandaria Returns to the Wider World

date.label: After the Cataclysm

events.summary: The long-hidden land of Pandaria became a theater of exploration and intensifying Alliance–Horde conflict.

events.name: The Pantheon Departs

date.label: After the ordering of Azeroth

events.summary: With Azeroth stabilized and its guardians appointed, the Pantheon departed while the keepers and titan-forged remained to watch over the world.

events.name: The Pantheon Discovers Azeroth

date.label: During the Black Empire's dominion

events.summary: Aggramar discovered Azeroth's nascent titan and the Old Gods rooted around it, bringing the imperiled world to the Pantheon's attention.

events.name: Gathering of the Pantheon

date.label: During Aman’Thul's search for other titans

events.summary: The awakened titans found one another, formed the Pantheon, and traveled onward to order worlds and seek more of their kind.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the Pantheon's formation in Chronicle Volume 1.

events.name: Emergence of the Physical Universe

date.label: At the beginning of Chronicle's cosmic account

events.summary: The conflict between primordial Light and Void gave rise to the physical universe, while released energies formed the Twisting Nether.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the creation sequence described in Chronicle Volume 1; it is not presented as a formally named Warcraft event.

events.name: The Plague Spreads Through Lordaeron

date.label: At the opening of the Third War

events.summary: A mysterious plague spread through Lordaeron as the Cult of the Damned and Scourge prepared the kingdom's destruction.

events.name: The Portal at the Well Collapses

date.label: At the end of the War of the Ancients

events.summary: The defenders disrupted the Legion's gateway before Sargeras could enter, and the unstable Well collapsed around the broken portal.

events.name: A hilt without a finder

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: In the Frozen Halls, a battered hilt may fall among the spoils of heroic danger. Its appearance is randomized game loot; no single finder belongs to history. The quest then brings the relic to Quel’Delar’s Rest, where the Silver Covenant or Sunreavers take up the question it carries. Before the sword is whole, its broken remnant has already drawn two rival courts toward the same inheritance.

events.name: The sword draws toward the Halls

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: From the frozen forge, Quel’Delar presses its bearer toward the Halls of Reflection. The quest frames this as compulsion: the blade has a will, and its direction leads into the Lich King’s chamber. This is a magical story beat, not a route inferred across a map. In the blue-black hall, the sword’s restoration turns inward. The first danger is no longer whether it can be wielded, but who commands whom.

events.name: A gift carried through generations

date.label: Before the Third War; exact date and ceremony location are not established here

events.summary: In the older account, Alexstrasza gives the blade to Anasterian, and the high king later entrusts it to Thalorien Dawnseeker. This is a remembered handoff, not a ceremony whose room or date the tale records. The Sunwell’s light fills this interpretive scene because the sword’s future defense is bound to Quel’Thalas. Its gold and red radiance now illuminates a gift moving toward its trial.

events.name: The name in the record

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; remembered history predates the quest

events.summary: Returned to the dragon’s record, the story of the hilt resolves into a name: Quel’Delar, sister to Quel’Serrar. Its remembered history binds red dragonflight craft to the high elven crown and to a defender who stood before the Sunwell. The book does not make the sword’s inheritance simple. It tells how a gift can outlive a kingdom’s wound, while leaving its next bearer to be contested.

events.name: A borrowed guise for old records

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: A disguise opens a way to records guarded by suspicion and old allegiances. The faction quest asks its chosen seeker to recover the ancient dragonforged blades’ history, not to invent a new forging tale. In this retelling, the folio is an interpretive emblem for that record. A successful theft is a game objective; the chronicle keeps the danger and purpose, not every repeated step of play.

events.name: The dragons weigh the risk

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: At Wyrmrest Temple, Krasus lends the seekers a record of the ancient blade. Kalecgos asks whether mortals should command such power: the dragons have known the grief of a mighty weapon turned against them. Alexstrasza permits the search to continue, though permission is not an answer to every fear. Beneath the red-bronze shrine, the hilt’s past begins to emerge as both a promise and a warning.

events.name: Two returns, no single heir

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest resolution; individual character choices vary

events.summary: The restored weapon returns to Dalaran by faction-specific roads. An Alliance seeker reports through Caladis and the Silver Covenant; a Horde seeker through Myralion and the Sunreavers. In the blood-elf sword branch, Aethas publicly presents the new bearer. Other characters unable to wield the sword receive a different weapon type. These are alternative game outcomes, not one champion’s combined history, and no named adventurer is made the canonical heir.

events.name: Tempered in the Forge of Souls

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: The newly joined blade travels to the Crucible of Souls, deep within the Forge of Souls. There it is tempered amid the machinery of the Lich King’s frozen halls. The glowing furnace is an interpretive setting for a named quest step, not a measured reconstruction of the dungeon room. The work succeeds in shaping the weapon, yet the next chamber reveals that a finished edge and a clean spirit are not the same thing.

events.name: A sacred shore must be approached

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: At Quel’Danas, Halduron Brightwing first refuses the seeker entry to a sacred place recently reclaimed by the blood elves. The Sunwell is no casual road’s end. Its shores carry the memory of a kingdom nearly lost, and trust must be earned before the blade can reach its light. Beyond the Dead Scar, pale stone and red-gold towers frame a question of stewardship: who may bring this dangerous inheritance to the well?

events.name: Lana’thel breaks the blade

date.label: Before the Wrath restoration quest; exact date unknown

events.summary: At Quel’Delar’s Rest, a more recent memory darkens the snow. Lana’thel recounts how the sword passed from Thalorien into her hands after his fall, and how, as the Lich King’s servant, she was ordered to destroy it. She carried Quel’Delar north and broke it here. Her account joins a knight’s last defense to a queen’s enslavement; the broken hilt at the quest’s opening is the remnant of that command.

events.name: Reforged in the Pit of Saron

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: In the Pit of Saron, the quest sets the old blade against saronite: five infused bars and a forgehammer remake its broken length. The mine is a place of forced labor beneath Icecrown, its black ore cut from a frozen wound. This is a player objective, not a separate campaign of named smiths. When the pieces are joined, the sword is whole again—but the material that holds it also carries a peril.

events.name: Orders in the violet city

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: In Dalaran, Caladis Brightspear and Myralion Sunblaze each direct their own faction’s search. Their orders are parallel branches in the quest, not a single council where both factions agree. The city’s pale towers and violet enchantments stand above a contest of memory: each side would restore the old blade, and each expects its own people to guard the inheritance.

events.name: Purified in the Sunwell

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: At last the tempered blade is lowered into the Sunwell. Light passes through the old steel and the saronite taint is cleansed; the quest presents a purified Quel’Delar where the corrupted weapon had rested. The well does not erase Lana’Thel’s command, Thalorien’s sacrifice, or the peril of the halls. It changes what can be carried forward. A weapon once broken and then remade leaves the sacred waters with a new claim upon the living.

events.name: Thalorien at the Sunwell gate

date.label: During the Third War, as the Scourge reached Quel’Thalas; exact date unknown

events.summary: When the Scourge reached Quel’Thalas, Thalorien held the approach before the Sunwell. He fell in that defense, buying time for those behind him; the quest’s memory binds his name to the blade he carried. The golden island was not spared its wound, and the champion was not carried into the future. His stand belongs to the Third War, long before this Wrath quest asks another hand to restore his sword.

events.name: A later trial at Thalorien’s rest

date.label: A later Wrath quest test at the remains of a Third War defender

events.summary: At Thalorien’s resting place, the Wrath quest sets a new seeker against a trial and a memory of the fallen knight. This encounter does not undo his death or make him a living participant in the restoration. His blessing links the blade’s old bearer to its present burden. The story holds both moments apart: Thalorien fell at the Sunwell in the Third War; a later test asks whether the seeker is worthy to carry his memory onward.

events.name: Two courts, one inheritance

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: At Quel’Delar’s Rest, an Alliance seeker answers Caladis Brightspear; a Horde seeker answers Myralion Sunblaze. Their plans pass through separate faction halls, and the player follows one allegiance, not both. In the city’s violet heights, old kinship between high and blood elves cannot settle who may claim the blade. The story keeps both roads visible as alternatives, without giving either branch a universal adventurer.

events.name: Uther names the taint

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: Uther’s spirit speaks beside the chamber’s blade: saronite is the blood of an Old God, and the ore has tainted what the hammer restored. His counsel turns the quest toward the Sunwell. No forging technique can cleanse this wound. Beyond the frozen halls lies a place of older light, reclaimed by the blood elves after its earlier fall. There, the sword’s makers’ legacy may be tested against the darkness forced into it.

events.name: A vow to make the blade whole

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: The sword’s breaking does not end its history. Myralion vows that the Sunreavers will restore it; Caladis leads the Silver Covenant along its separate path. The two representatives are shown here as a comparative split scene, not as companions sharing one event. Their promise gives purpose to the work ahead: remake the blade, face the will bound within it, and seek a cleansing strong enough to remove what the Scourge has left.

events.name: The blade’s will is subdued

date.label: Wrath of the Lich King, patch 3.3.5 quest sequence; exact in-world date unknown

events.summary: The seeker resists the sword’s command and brings its will to heel. Quel’Delar survives the struggle; neither its steel nor the story’s inherited name is discarded. Yet victory in the Halls of Reflection is only restraint. The blade was reforged with the dark ore of Icecrown, and a quieted weapon may still bear the touch of the place that shaped it. A voice from the chamber names the deeper danger.

events.name: Quel'Thalas and the Sunwell Are Founded

date.label: Approximately 6,800 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: The exiles established Quel'Thalas in the northern Eastern Kingdoms and created the Sunwell as the heart of their new civilization.

events.name: Quel'Thalas and the Sunwell Fall

date.label: During the Scourge advance after Lordaeron's fall

events.summary: The Scourge broke Quel'Thalas, raised Sylvanas into undeath, and corrupted the Sunwell while advancing its larger design.

events.name: Quel'Thalas and Arathor Form a Wartime Alliance

date.label: During the Troll Wars

events.summary: Facing an overwhelming Amani assault, Quel'Thalas allied with Arathor and shared limited arcane instruction in exchange for military aid.

events.name: Ragnaros Re-emerges at Blackrock

date.label: At the end of the War of the Three Hammers

events.summary: A desperate Dark Iron summoning brought Ragnaros back into the world, devastated the southern mountains, and ended the dwarven war beneath a new volcanic power.

events.name: The key and the armies

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The three recovered fragments returned to the bronze dragon, and the scepter could be made whole. Beyond that personal journey, Horde and Alliance communities were gathering the supplies for a campaign in Silithus. The key alone was not the war effort. Workshops, stores and countless contributions prepared the force that would have to stand before the opened stronghold. Rival peoples worked toward the same threshold, without losing the histories that divided them. The coming battle required both the recovered artifact and the many hands that no single quest could name.

events.name: Blue shard — A dragon who wished to be left alone

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: On Azshara's coast, Azuregos offered a very different account of guardianship. The shard had drawn attention he did not want, interrupting his study of the ancient shore. He had hidden it with an enchanted fish, making an ordinary search of the sea hopeless. His solution for its recovery was an arcanite buoy that would draw the creature out. The instructions lay in a ledger, and the ledger had to be taken to Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris. The blue trail began with a dragon's evasion and became an engineer's problem.

events.name: Beyond the wall, beneath the temple

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The campaign continued into the Ruins and the Temple of Ahn'Qiraj. Beyond the qiraji armies lay C'Thun, the deeper threat against which the preparations had been gathered. Victory there gave the opened gate its purpose: the company had not restored a key merely to release what waited behind the wall. It had restored a way to reach that danger. The victory brought this campaign to its close, after a long road from the bronze dragon’s vigil. The scepter's legacy joins the losses of the first war to the collective labor of the second.

events.name: Red shard — Beyond the dragon’s suffering

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The red trail ended with Nefarian's defeat and the recovery of the fragment before it could be destroyed. When it was brought back to Anachronos, the bronze dragon spoke of Vaelastrasz's soul finding rest. The shard was not merely a treasure won from a raid. Its return fulfilled the charge of a guardian whose own strength had failed him. One piece of the scepter was recovered, but the cost of its keeping remained part of the story that the restored artifact would carry.

events.name: Blue shard — The chef and the Isle of Dread

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: Another of Narain's demands led to Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan. The chef's answer sent the adventurers out to the Isle of Dread, off Feralas, to hunt the chimaerok and secure the ingredients for his formidable meal. The scale of the task belonged to the same curious bargain as the goggles: the world's key depended upon satisfying the engineer's requirements. This branch brought the search from desert workshops to a dangerous island, where even preparing a feast called for allies rather than a solitary traveler.

events.name: Blue shard — Libraries, demons, and dragon lairs

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The missing chapters drew the adventurers through places that rarely belonged to one journey. Pages awaited in Stormwind and Undercity, in the dangerous reaches of Winterspring and the Blasted Lands, and on Doctor Weavil's Alcaz Island. Others required the company to return to Blackwing Lair, confront Onyxia, and reach Ragnaros in Molten Core. A single scattered volume bound these distant dangers to the same unfinished work. The reconstructed volume gave Narain the means to continue the work Azuregos had set before him.

events.name: Green shard — The guardian returns

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: Tyrande's arrival brought the intervention the defenders had awaited. Eranikus was redeemed, and Remulos spoke of his return to the Dream to confront the wrong he had done. The green fragment could now be carried back to Anachronos. Unlike the red trail, this recovery left its guardian able to return to his own work. The two journeys shared a broken scepter, but their endings were different: one honored a lost watcher; the other restored a watcher to the struggle from which he had fallen.

events.name: Green shard — The gathering of corruption

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: Remulos's preparations sent the adventurers to the forest portals associated with the Dream. The search ranged through Duskwood, Ashenvale, Feralas and the Hinterlands, gathering the fragments needed for the next confrontation. These were separate places bound by one danger, rather than a single road across the forest. The journey widened the threat beyond the temple where it had begun. By returning with the corruption's traces, the seekers made possible the attempt to draw Eranikus into Moonglade, where his redemption could be sought.

events.name: Green shard — A guardian lost to the Nightmare

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The green trail began beneath the marshes, in the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. Near the Shade of Eranikus, Malfurion's appearance directed the search beyond the temple and toward his agent in Teldrassil. From the forest wisp, the road led to Keeper Remulos in Moonglade. The green shard could not be reclaimed by treating its guardian as another enemy to be slain. The search had reached a dragon ensnared by the Nightmare, and the help it sought would have to reach him through that corruption.

events.name: The memory at the Scarab Wall

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: Before seeking the scattered pieces, the adventurers returned to the place where the bond had broken. At the Scarab Wall, the old struggle was shown again: dragons pressing back the qiraji, defenders reaching the barrier, and Fandral turning away from the offered key. This was no new battle in Silithus. It was the past made visible to those who would inherit its unfinished task. The scepter could open a gate; the memory explained why that gate had first been closed, and why its key had been rejected.

events.name: Blue shard — From Silverpine to Molten Core

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: Narain could not turn the ledger into a finished answer without further help. His missing scrying goggles led the seekers to Stewvul, his former friend, hiding in a crate near the Greymane Wall in Silverpine. Stewvul no longer had them: the search continued into Molten Core. Thus a quarrel between gnomes carried the greater quest beneath Blackrock Mountain. The equipment had to be recovered before Narain's work could proceed, binding an apparently small personal errand to the fate of the unopened gates.

events.name: Blue shard — The beast in the Bay of Storms

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: With the preparations complete, the blue trail returned to the sea. Narain sent the adventurers to the Bay of Storms in Azshara with the arcanite buoy, warning them of Maws. The creature that held the shard could be drawn from hiding, but recovering it demanded companions ready for the danger that answered. When the blue fragment was won, the instructions were at last simple: carry it to Anachronos. An old dragon's elaborate concealment had become a journey through much of Azeroth before ending on its storm-bound coast.

events.name: Green shard — Restraint at Nighthaven

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: When Eranikus entered Nighthaven, the duty was to endure him, not to kill him. Keeper Remulos had to survive, and the settlement had to be defended while Tyrande approached. The dragon's assault and the shades of the Nightmare made that restraint costly. Yet destroying him would defeat the purpose for which the defenders had gathered. Their task was to hold the space in which rescue remained possible: to stand against his violence without surrendering the hope that the guardian beneath it could be freed.

events.name: Blue shard — A ransom in the snow

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The search for Narain's book brought back a ransom letter instead of the missing volume. Its captors demanded payment, and Narain answered with a deception of his own. He gave the adventurers clothing to take his place and a sack of rocks to stand for gold. The appointed meeting lay in Winterspring, far from his desert home. There the false payment brought the seekers into the encounter with Number Two. The scheme did not recover the book; its pages still had to be gathered by another road.

events.name: Flashback · Era 5 — A victory without comfort

date.label: Ancient War of the Shifting Sands

events.summary: At the gate, Merithra, Arygos and Caelestrasz held the enemy back while Anachronos and the defenders raised the barrier. When the seal was made, the bronze dragon offered Fandral a scepter and a gong: a means to open the way if the need returned. Fandral would accept no further burden from that victory. His son was gone; the stronghold still stood. He cast the scepter against the barrier and shattered it. Anachronos gathered the fragments, preserving a duty that grief had refused.

events.name: The road from Cenarion Hold

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The later journey began in Silithus, where Baristolth of the Shifting Sands directed seekers toward the bronze dragon at the Caverns of Time. Anachronos did not simply place the world's burden in the first hands that reached him. The path demanded evidence of resolve. It led into Blackwing Lair, to Broodlord Lashlayer, before the deeper work of gaining the brood's trust. The task was already larger than one traveler: a champion's progress depended upon companions willing to enter the mountain together.

events.name: Flashback · Era 5 — The war that raised the wall

date.label: Ancient War of the Shifting Sands

events.summary: Long before the adventurers came to Silithus, the night elves had fought a war beneath its harsh southern sky. Fandral Staghelm led their defense against the qiraji, and his son Valstann fell in the struggle. The dragonflights joined the battle, but neither courage nor ancient power could make the loss undone. As the defenders were driven toward Ahn'Qiraj, the question before them became how to contain an enemy they could not wholly destroy. The wall that later generations would find was born of that necessity.

events.name: The gates open

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: When the preparations had brought the campaign to the Scarab Wall, the restored scepter could be raised against the gong. The barrier made by the ancient defenders opened, and the danger it had contained came forth. The ensuing struggle was remembered as the Ten-Hour War. The relic's recovery had not ended the conflict; it had made the confrontation possible. Where Fandral once turned away from the gate in grief, a later generation now stood together before the consequences of opening it.

events.name: Red shard — The captive guardian

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: In Blackwing Lair, Vaelastrasz could no longer fulfill his charge by surrendering the red shard. Nefarian held it, and threatened to destroy it. The wounded red dragon's appeal made the recovery urgent: the loss of that fragment would deny the seekers their key to Ahn'Qiraj. Here the search for an ancient relic entered a living act of cruelty. The adventurers had to carry Vaelastrasz's last request through the fortress of the very enemy who had brought him low.

events.name: The keepers of a broken promise

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The broken scepter did not pass out of history. Its pieces remained in the keeping of dragons, yet the long vigil brought troubles of its own. When Anachronos later named Eranikus, Vaelastrasz and Azuregos, his warning carried the weight of disappointed trust. Each guardian's story had turned toward tragedy or estrangement. To restore the key, mortal seekers would have to enter those stories. A thousand years separated the wars, but time had not protected the watchers from the wounds of the world.

events.name: The journey that outlived the gong

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: The gong belonged to a brief opening in the campaign, but the quest's final recognition was not identical to that moment. Treasure of the Timeless One remained a distinct conclusion for those who held the restored scepter after the opening war. Remembering that distinction keeps the journey larger than a race for a title. Across forests, libraries, mountains and seas, the work had gathered companions around a broken promise. Its completion remembered the long recovery, as well as the threshold that recovery had allowed the world to cross.

events.name: Blue shard — A book scattered to the winds

date.label: Original WoW Scepter quest journey

events.summary: Narain's missing volume of Draconic for Dummies became another obstacle. Doctor Weavil had intervened, and the book was torn into eight chapters. Narain supplied a magical binding, but the scattered pages had to be found before the volume could be made whole. The search now reached far beyond Tanaris. A text needed to understand the ledger became a second broken object within the greater quest: before the dragon's key could be restored, the engineer's book had to be restored as well.

events.name: The Second War Begins

date.label: After the formation of the Alliance of Lordaeron

events.summary: The Horde drove north while the newly formed Alliance organized a defense across several kingdoms and theaters.

events.name: The Covenant Campaigns Converge

date.label: During the Shadowlands campaign

events.summary: Champions worked among distinct covenant realms whose campaigns formed the broad framework of resistance in the afterlife.

events.name: Shattrath Falls to the Horde

date.label: Near the culmination of the Horde's war against the draenei

events.summary: The Horde's assault devastated Shattrath and broke the principal center of organized draenei resistance, though draenei survivors endured.

events.name: The Siege Ends Garrosh's Rule

date.label: At the end of the Pandaria conflict

events.summary: Opposition from within and beyond the Horde converged on Orgrimmar and ended Garrosh Hellscream's rule.

events.name: The Primordial Imbalance

date.label: Before the arrival of the Old Gods

events.summary: As Azeroth's world-soul developed, it consumed much of the fifth element, Spirit, leaving the native elementals without its balancing influence.
events.description: This descriptive event record captures the source account’s causal explanation for the violent state of primordial Azeroth's elementals.

events.name: Stormwind Falls

date.label: At the end of the First War

events.summary: The Horde captured and devastated Stormwind, forcing surviving leaders and refugees to flee north.

events.name: Stratholme Is Purged

date.label: After the plague is discovered in Lordaeron

events.summary: Convinced Stratholme's people were infected, Arthas ordered the city purged; Jaina and Uther rejected the course, deepening his isolation.

events.name: The Sunwell Becomes the Darkwell

date.label: During the Voidspire confrontation

events.summary: Xal’atath channels Void power into the Sunwell, transforming it into the Darkwell as Alleria and Turalyon vanish into its depths.
events.description: The timeline records their disappearance, not a confirmed ultimate fate.

events.name: Survivors Reach Mount Hyjal

date.label: Immediately after the Great Sundering

events.summary: Many surviving defenders reached the lands around Mount Hyjal, carrying the memory of the lost world into the beginning of the Long Vigil.

events.name: Thoradin Unites Arathor

date.label: Approximately 2,800 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Thoradin brought scattered human tribes beneath one banner and established Arathor around the fortified center of Strom.

events.name: Thrall Liberates Interned Orcs

date.label: Nearly thirteen years after the Horde's defeat

events.summary: Thrall freed orcs from internment and gathered a new Horde whose purpose was not identical to the conquered Old Horde.

events.name: A family restored in paint

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The returned painting brings Karandra and young Taelan into view beside Tirion. The Classic quest connects it to family outings and a portrait made by Renfray; the lakeside colors here interpret that recollection rather than claim an exact beach or the canvas’s original appearance. The painting restores a likeness, not a lost childhood. For Tirion, memory can now be given back in a form his son may recognize, if the son is still willing to receive it.

events.name: A gift beneath Scarlet colors

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: A disguise opens the way into Hearthglen, where Tirion’s gift can reach Taelan. The Classic chain makes subterfuge the bridge between father and son: the seeker enters the Scarlet Crusade’s stronghold under borrowed colors and gives the package to its Highlord. The banners and pale stone of the settlement frame a tense reunion without placing Tirion there. The audience sees the old family tokens cross a guarded threshold; what Taelan will do with them remains his choice.

events.name: A vow to rebuild the Silver Hand

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: At Taelan’s body, Tirion vows to gather a new Order of the Silver Hand and turn it again toward the defense of the world. The Classic chain ends with a purpose, not with the later history of that order already fulfilled. A small emblem rests beside the grieving father as a visual echo of the honor Taelan once laid down. The quest closes Tirion and Taelan’s story here; later campaigns, including the Wrath-era chapters, belong to their own records.

events.name: The road ends at the tower

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Beyond Hearthglen, the quest brings Taelan to a roadside tower and Grand Inquisitor Isillien. It records Taelan’s death there at Isillien’s hands. The story does not soften this into a mere interruption: the son who chose to leave the Scarlet Crusade has no return to the father he hoped to meet. The tower stands at the edge of the road, a small human post amid a wounded land, and the long effort to restore memory reaches its cost.

events.name: Myranda at Uther’s Tomb

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The keepsakes travel onward as a message to Myranda, whom the chain locates at Uther’s Tomb. Tirion asks his former ally to help the seeker pass into Hearthglen. Myranda’s brief place in this story reaches back to her work alongside him, though this quest does not retell every part of her life. Against pale memorial stone and plague-damaged grass, she becomes the last guide before the family’s past is carried directly to Taelan.

events.name: Out through Hearthglen

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Taelan leaves the keep and makes his way out through Hearthglen. The quest turns this departure into an ordeal as Scarlet Crusade forces oppose him. He is no longer the quiet child Tirion watched from exile: he has chosen to break with the order that shaped his adult life. The guards become a last barrier between the Highlord and the open road. The chain gives no private motive to each soldier, and Taelan’s struggle ends at the tower beyond the settlement.

events.name: Renfray remembers Caer Darrow

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Tirion’s memory turns from the marks of duty to family excursions and an artist’s work. He sends the seeker to Caer Darrow, where his old friend Artist Renfray remains among the ruins. She painted the Fordring family in happier days. The island is now a quiet ruin in the lake, and Renfray is a ghost; the quest asks for a portrait, not a return to the life it preserves. Across years of exile, the canvas is a rare piece of the family’s past that has not vanished.

events.name: Taelan ends the dream

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The gift reaches the part of Taelan that his title could not silence. In the quest account, he recognizes how long he has been made a tool of the Grand Crusader, and his father’s memory has endured beneath that service. Taelan decides to leave Hearthglen. The portrait and keepsakes do not command him; they return a past from which he can make a choice of his own. The hall’s red-and-white standards still surround him, but their claim on his future has broken.

events.name: A small hammer beneath a false grave

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: A miniature warhammer, once given to Taelan by his father, lies in the Undercroft. The reproduced quest account connects it to a false grave and to the story Taelan had been told as a child: that Tirion was dead. The object is small enough for a young hand, but it carries the weight of an absence made permanent by a lie. Its recovery does not undo the years apart. It gives Tirion one remembered gift to place before his son.

events.name: The old hermit by Thondroril

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: In the cold reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, an old hermit accepts help before he offers his name. The early errands are practical work among the dangers of the plague-struck countryside; they prove only that a stranger can be trusted. The narration begins at the bank where the hermit waits, after those tasks have opened his story. They did not cause his exile, and they are not recast here as a single battle. Beyond the river, a family’s long absence is the wound still waiting to be named.

events.name: The emblem in Northdale’s lake

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Tirion next asks for a symbol Taelan left behind. The quest recalls his son’s stand at Northdale after Uther’s death and says Taelan laid down the Silver Hand standard; its emblem now lies beneath the lake. The record preserves a moment of disillusion, not a full account of the fighting. We do not invent an exact battlefield line or name the soldiers who stood with him. The small sign of the old order rises from dark water, ready to join the hammer as a piece of shared history.

events.name: The portrait behind the twin moons

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Renfray’s follow-up bears the same title as the task that brought the seeker to her, yet it is a different Classic quest. Its objective leads into Stratholme, where the family painting is hidden behind a picture of twin moons in the Archivist’s room. The crimson city has become a storehouse of other people’s ruin; within it, a small work of family memory survives. This scene shows the concealment as an original interpretation, not an exact dungeon plan or verified painting model.

events.name: Tirion arrives

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: Tirion reaches the tower too late to save his son. The quest account then has him defeat Isillien and grieve beside Taelan. The father’s return answers the appeal he made at Thondroril, but not in the way he sought: he has recovered the truth and lost the living voice that might have answered him. We hold the scene to those recorded actions. No dialogue is reconstructed, and the art does not invent a private final exchange.

events.name: The father in exile

date.label: Original World of Warcraft Classic · Tirion and Taelan quest chain; exact dating unknown

events.summary: The hermit names himself Tirion Fordring. The quest account says that he was convicted of treason and banished from the Alliance; it does not explain the charge’s full history. He chose to remain in exile near his son. Taelan became lord of Mardenholde and later a Highlord of the Scarlet Crusade, an order Tirion sees as fallen from the Silver Hand’s purpose. Tirion asks for help because he believes his son can still remember the honor they once shared.

events.name: The Titan-forged Are Mustered

date.label: After direct intervention wounded Azeroth

events.summary: The Pantheon created armies of stone and metal and empowered the greatest among them as keepers to lead the war for Azeroth.

events.name: Turalyon Rallies the Alliance

date.label: Immediately after Lothar's death

events.summary: Turalyon rallied the shaken Alliance and sustained the counteroffensive that drove the Horde south.

events.name: The Veil into the Shadowlands Is Shattered

date.label: At the opening of the Shadowlands crisis

events.summary: Sylvanas shattered the veil between life and death, drawing champions into the Shadowlands and its covenant realms.

events.name: The War Within Opens in Khaz Algar

date.label: Opening chapter of the Worldsoul Saga

events.summary: Xal'atath's gathering threat led champions into Khaz Algar and its subterranean worlds, where the Earthen became central allies and witnesses.

events.name: The World-wound Is Stabilized

date.label: After the surviving Old Gods were imprisoned

events.summary: The keepers raised wards around Azeroth's bleeding wound until its arcane energies settled into the Well of Eternity.

events.name: Ancient Allies Join the Defense

date.label: During the widening War of the Ancients

events.summary: Cenarius and other powers of ancient Kalimdor joined the defense, while the Dragon Aspects prepared a weapon intended to drive back the Legion.

events.name: The World-forges Are Established

date.label: During the healing of Azeroth

events.summary: The keepers established complementary facilities in the far north and south to stabilize Azeroth and sustain the work of ordering it.

events.name: The Removal of Y'Shaarj

date.label: At the beginning of the Pantheon's intervention

events.summary: Aman’Thul tore Y'Shaarj from Azeroth, destroying the Old God but opening a terrible wound in the sleeping world-soul.

battles.name: The Battle of Mount Hyjal

date.label: At the culmination of the Third War

battles.summary: A temporary coalition delayed Archimonde's advance long enough for Malfurion to call upon Nordrassil's power and destroy him.
battles.description: This dossier treats Mount Hyjal as an era-defining strategic defense. Its phases explain convergence, delay, and outcome without replaying Warcraft III missions or asserting exact camps and troop paths.

objectives.summary: Reach Nordrassil and seize the power gathered at Mount Hyjal.
Delay the Legion's advance and preserve the mountain long enough for a final answer.

phases.title: The Legion turns toward the mountain
phases.summary: Archimonde drives the invasion toward Mount Hyjal and Nordrassil.
phases.narration: The northern kingdoms had already paid the price of the Scourge's design. In Kalimdor, the Legion now bent its strength toward the crown of the mountain and the power rooted there.

phases.title: Old enemies accept one defense
phases.summary: Night elves, New Horde forces, and Alliance survivors converge under a temporary common purpose.
phases.narration: No single people could hold the road alone. Those who had met as strangers and rivals gathered beneath one necessity, retaining their own names even as they took their places in a shared defense.

phases.title: The ascent is made costly
phases.summary: The defenders yield ground while buying the time on which the mountain's survival depends.
phases.narration: This was not a clean wall drawn across the land. It was delay purchased in stages, positions abandoned only after time had been wrested from the invader and carried upward toward Nordrassil.

phases.title: Archimonde reaches for Nordrassil
phases.summary: The Legion commander reaches the World Tree as Malfurion's final response gathers.
phases.narration: Archimonde climbed within reach of the ancient tree. The long defense had not barred every step; it had created the moment in which another kind of strength could answer him.

phases.title: The tree's gathered power is released
phases.summary: Malfurion calls upon Nordrassil's power; Archimonde is destroyed and the invasion is broken.
phases.narration: At the last height, Malfurion called upon the power gathered around Nordrassil. Archimonde was destroyed. Victory did not restore the kingdoms already fallen, but it broke the Legion's assault and left the survivors to shape what came after.

outcome.summary: The coalition delayed the advance until Nordrassil's released power destroyed Archimonde, ending the Legion's immediate invasion while leaving the northern kingdoms transformed.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Mount Hyjal and Nordrassil are broadly located, but the conflict comprised several defensive positions whose exact mission geography is not asserted here.

battles.name: The Elemental Assault on the Black Empire

date.label: After the Black Empire began to spread

battles.summary: For the first time, Azeroth's rival elemental hosts united against the Old Gods and attacked the Black Empire's growing cities.
battles.description: This descriptive title groups a broad conflict rather than asserting one localized battle. The cited account describes firestorms and stone barriers striking Black Empire cities but does not provide mappable routes.

objectives.summary: Remove the Old Gods and their growing civilization from Azeroth.
Preserve and expand the Old Gods' domains through n'raqi and aqir forces.

phases.title: Rivals unite
phases.summary: The four elemental powers recognized a common threat.
phases.narration: As the Black Empire widened its shadow, the ancient enemies understood at last that none could stand alone. For the first time, Azeroth's elemental powers gathered against one foe.

phases.title: Firestorms cross the empire
phases.summary: Air and fire combined against Black Empire cities.
phases.narration: Wind and flame went forth together. Al'Akir's tempests bore the wrath of Ragnaros across the dark dominion, and immense firestorms descended upon the empire's citadels.

phases.title: Stone closes around the cities
phases.summary: Therazane raised barriers against the empire's settlements.
phases.narration: Then Therazane laid her strength upon the field. Jagged walls rose at her bidding, hemming in the servants of the Old Gods and breaking against their temple cities.

phases.title: The servant hosts endure
phases.summary: The empire answered through the n'raqi and aqir.
phases.narration: Yet from the cities came the n'raqi and the innumerable aqir. Rank after rank endured the elemental fury, until even the joined hosts could not overcome them.

phases.title: The resistance fails
phases.summary: The Old Gods defeated and enslaved the Elemental Lords.
phases.narration: In the end the resistance was broken. The Old Gods bound the Elemental Lords, and with no native power left to bar its way, the Black Empire spread across much of the world.

outcome.summary: The elemental resistance failed; the Elemental Lords were enslaved and the Black Empire extended its dominion over much of Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The conflict covered multiple unnamed sites. No exact marker or route is asserted.

battles.name: The Elemental Wars

date.label: Untold ages before the Old Gods' arrival

battles.summary: The four Elemental Lords and their hosts fought across primordial Azeroth for ages, with dominion shifting continually and no lasting victor.
battles.description: The title is a descriptive grouping for the source account’s world-spanning elemental conflict. Because the source supplies no stable front or exact battlefield, the atlas records its geography as unknown.

objectives.summary: Each rival elemental host sought dominion and the remaking of the world in its own image.

phases.title: The winds divide
phases.summary: Al'Akir weakened rivals through spies, deception, and sudden storms.
phases.narration: From the high airs Al'Akir watched the wars below. Through spies and deception he divided his enemies, and his tempests fell only when rival strength had already been spent.

phases.title: Fire overwhelms
phases.summary: Ragnaros answered strategy with volcanic, direct destruction.
phases.narration: Ragnaros placed no faith in subtle designs. Before him volcanoes opened, fire crowned the land, and ash followed where his overwhelming host had passed.

phases.title: Earth endures
phases.summary: Therazane sheltered behind mountains and counterattacked exhausted enemies.
phases.narration: Therazane gathered her children behind the strength of mountains. There they endured the fury of their foes, and only when the assault was weary did the earth rise to answer.

phases.title: Water divides and conquers
phases.summary: Neptulon waited for rival armies to separate before crushing them.
phases.narration: Neptulon did not squander his waters against a gathered host. He waited until the armies of his foes were divided, then loosed the deep against them in their weakness.

outcome.summary: No permanent victor emerged; control shifted while the conflict continued for untold ages.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Chronicle describes a world-spanning conflict without exact battle sites or stable fronts, so no marker or route is drawn.

battles.name: The First War

date.label: From the opening of the Dark Portal through the fall of Stormwind

battles.summary: A multi-year invasion in which the Old Horde crossed from Draenor, fought the Kingdom of Stormwind, changed leadership, and ultimately captured the southern capital.
battles.description: This dossier presents an atlas-scale strategic sequence. The source chapter supports repeated offensives, political upheaval, and Stormwind's fall, but not one exact battlefield or a complete surveyed route assembled from game missions.

objectives.summary: Establish the invasion on Azeroth and break the Kingdom of Stormwind.
Contain the invaders, preserve the kingdom, and uncover the power enabling the portal.

phases.title: A new enemy crosses the threshold
phases.summary: Horde forces emerge from the Dark Portal and begin probing the southern kingdom.
phases.narration: The first crossings did not reveal the full weight waiting beyond the gate. They were enough to turn a hidden act of sorcery into war and to teach Stormwind that the enemy had no homeland upon its maps.

phases.title: Stormwind survives the first blows
phases.summary: The defenders resist early attacks while the Horde learns the land and gathers greater strength.
phases.narration: The kingdom did not fall at the first alarm. Resistance bought time, but each return carried greater confidence, while fear and uncertainty divided those who still believed the war could be contained.

phases.title: The hand behind the gate is uncovered
phases.summary: Stormwind's defenders discover Medivh's role, severing the Azeroth-side will that had enabled the invasion.
phases.narration: The road of the invasion led inward as well as east. The Guardian who should have watched the world had helped open it, and stopping him ended one design without recalling the armies already across the threshold.

phases.title: The Horde changes masters
phases.summary: Orgrim kills Blackhand, attacks the Shadow Council's power, and assumes command.
phases.narration: The invaders' unity concealed another war. Orgrim struck down Blackhand and tore at the council behind him. The Horde changed masters, yet its armies remained upon Azeroth and its hunger for victory did not depart with the old warchief.

phases.title: The southern kingdom is broken
phases.summary: The Horde captures Stormwind and surviving leaders carry warning north.
phases.narration: At last the southern walls failed. Victory gave the Horde a ruined capital, while the sea carried survivors and a warning toward kingdoms that had not yet understood that Stormwind's war would soon become their own.

outcome.summary: Stormwind was captured and devastated, the First War ended in Horde victory, and survivors escaped north to seek a wider alliance.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The First War comprised many movements and engagements. No single exact battlefield point is asserted; the displayed route is explicitly inferred.

battles.name: The Fourth War Campaign

date.label: After the Legion's defeat

battles.summary: A strategic dossier of the faction war's widening fronts, internal rebellion, and political conclusion.
battles.description: The dossier avoids reproducing mission routes or reducing a global war to one precise marker.

phases.title: The war spreads through distant footholds
phases.summary: Both factions establish campaigns across new fronts.
phases.narration: The wounded world received another war, its ships and armies carrying old mistrust into lands already rich with histories of their own.

phases.title: Each victory enlarges the debt
phases.summary: The conflict's reprisals and campaigns deepen its human and political cost.
phases.narration: Territory changed hands; grief did not. Every answered wound became an argument for the next.

phases.title: The Horde fractures around its leadership
phases.summary: Opposition to Sylvanas grows within the Horde.
phases.narration: Within the Horde, loyalty to a people and obedience to a ruler no longer pointed along the same road.

phases.title: Opposition converges
phases.summary: Horde rebels and Alliance pressure align against Sylvanas's rule.
phases.narration: Those who had stood on opposite sides of the war arrived at one gate with purposes that overlapped, though their losses did not become one story.

phases.title: The campaign ends; its consequences remain
phases.summary: Sylvanas departs and the Fourth War campaign closes.
phases.narration: The banners lowered before the memories beneath them. An ending to the campaign was not an undoing of what the campaign had made.

outcome.summary: The rebellion and Alliance pressure ended Sylvanas's rule and closed the Fourth War campaign.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The Fourth War spanned many theaters and is not assigned a false single battlefield.

battles.name: The Frozen Throne Campaign

date.label: After the Battle of Mount Hyjal

battles.summary: A cross-world sequence in which Illidan established power in Outland, returned to strike Icecrown, and lost the final race to Arthas.
battles.description: The dossier links Outland and Icecrown through deterministic map-state changes. Each world keeps local coordinates, and no false geographic route is drawn between them.

objectives.summary: Build the strength to assault Icecrown and destroy the Frozen Throne.
Reach and preserve the Frozen Throne before Illidan's coalition can break it.

phases.title: Illidan turns exile into a campaign
phases.summary: Illidan and his allies close portals within Outland and challenge its existing ruler.
phases.narration: Beyond Azeroth, Illidan made refuge into preparation. His coalition moved through a broken world, closing the roads by which greater powers might follow and gathering strength beneath an alien sky.

phases.title: A new power rises in Outland
phases.summary: The coalition overthrows Magtheridon's rule and establishes a base for the next command.
phases.narration: The shattered world did not become whole beneath new masters. Yet its balance changed. Illidan stood at the center of a coalition held together by need, ambition, and the enemies waiting beyond it.

phases.title: The contest returns to Azeroth
phases.summary: Illidan's forces and Arthas move toward Icecrown from different purposes and paths.
phases.narration: The next road cannot be drawn across the void between worlds. The atlas therefore changes states: Outland recedes, Icecrown rises, and two purposes narrow toward the same throne.

phases.title: The last passage is contested
phases.summary: Illidan reaches Icecrown but Arthas defeats him before the Frozen Throne.
phases.narration: At Icecrown the broad campaign became a final contest. Illidan's assault failed before the throne could be destroyed, and the way above remained open to Arthas.

phases.title: Arthas climbs into a new order
phases.summary: Arthas reaches the Frozen Throne and becomes the Lich King.
phases.narration: Arthas climbed the last height and took the Frozen Throne's power into himself. The prince who had ridden out to save a kingdom now presided over the force that had destroyed it, and a darker inheritance passed into the coming age.

outcome.summary: Illidan's assault failed; Arthas reached the Frozen Throne and became the Lich King, establishing a new power inherited by the Age of Adventurers.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The campaign spans separate worldspaces and broad theaters. Only local inferred routes are shown, never a line between Outland and Azeroth.

battles.name: The Icecrown Citadel Campaign

date.label: At the culmination of the Northrend campaign

battles.summary: A broad strategic dossier tracing the coalition's advance through Icecrown to the fall of Arthas as the Lich King.
battles.description: These phases summarize campaign logic rather than raid encounters or exact troop movements.

objectives.summary: Preserve the Lich King's dominion from Icecrown.
Break the Scourge's northern power and confront the Lich King.

phases.title: The war reaches Northrend
phases.summary: Coalition forces establish the long campaign's northern front.
phases.narration: Across the cold sea, armies and wandering companies entered a land already shaped by the throne above it.

phases.title: The Scourge yields no easy road
phases.summary: The campaign crosses a continent of entrenched undead power.
phases.narration: Every road northward bore the memory of older defeats, and every victory narrowed the distance to their author.

phases.title: Icecrown Citadel is breached
phases.summary: The assault enters the seat of the Lich King's rule.
phases.narration: At the glacier's crown, the campaign passed from a war across land into a reckoning within the citadel itself.

phases.title: The throne receives its challengers
phases.summary: Champions confront Arthas at the center of his power.
phases.narration: The lost prince stood where an age before he had claimed the crown; those who climbed to him carried the cost of all the years between.

phases.title: Arthas's reign ends
phases.summary: The Lich King's immediate reign is broken, though Northrend's burden is not made simple.
phases.narration: The king fell. The ice did not forget him, and victory did not turn the dead back into the living, but the long command from Icecrown was ended.

outcome.summary: Arthas was defeated at Icecrown and his reign as the Lich King ended.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Icecrown is broadly placed; dossier phases do not assert exact landings, formations, or encounter positions.

battles.name: The Second War

date.label: After Stormwind's fall through the destruction of the original Dark Portal

battles.summary: A multi-theater war in which the Horde drove north against the Alliance of Lordaeron before internal fracture and an Alliance counteroffensive reversed the campaign.
battles.description: The dossier describes strategic direction and leadership changes rather than replaying missions or simulating units. Land, sea, and aerial theaters are condensed into two explicitly inferred atlas routes.

objectives.summary: Break the northern coalition and secure lasting Horde dominion on Azeroth.
Stop the northern offensive, liberate occupied lands, and close the gateway that sustains the invasion.

phases.title: The Horde drives north
phases.summary: Orgrim leads a broad offensive from the conquered south toward the Alliance kingdoms.
phases.narration: Stormwind's fall had opened the road but not ended resistance. The Horde drove north across many theaters, while a coalition still new to itself learned to answer as more than seven separate fears.

phases.title: The coalition becomes an army
phases.summary: Lothar coordinates the Alliance while its members defend several threatened realms.
phases.narration: Alliance was first a promise spoken under approaching danger. Campaign made it practice. Different peoples, commanders, and interests held together because none could afford the loneliness in which Stormwind had fallen.

phases.title: The northern kingdoms face the invasion
phases.summary: The Horde campaign threatens the Alliance heartlands but does not secure a final victory.
phases.narration: The war reached lands that had once heard Stormwind's ruin as distant news. Yet breadth became a burden as well as strength: every new front lengthened the purpose holding the Horde together.

phases.title: Ambition divides the offensive
phases.summary: Gul'dan removes forces from the campaign for his own purpose, weakening the Horde.
phases.narration: The hidden bargain at the Horde's birth had never produced one purpose. Gul'dan turned away at the hour of greatest need, and the strength taken from the main host opened a fracture no command could simply close.

phases.title: A commander falls and an army rises
phases.summary: Lothar dies near Blackrock Spire; Turalyon rallies the Alliance rather than allowing it to break.
phases.narration: Near Blackrock, the Alliance lost the man who had carried Stormwind's warning north. Grief might have ended the advance. Turalyon made it a summons, and the army moved again with its memory before it.

phases.title: The tide returns toward the gate
phases.summary: The Alliance drives the weakened Horde south from Blackrock toward the Dark Portal.
phases.narration: The road of invasion reversed. The coalition that had formed from one kingdom's ruin passed through Blackrock and pressed south, while the Horde's remaining order narrowed around retreat and survival.

phases.title: The gateway is broken
phases.summary: The Alliance defeats the Horde at the threshold and destroys the original Dark Portal.
phases.narration: At the threshold between worlds, victory closed the road but not its consequences. The portal fell, many orcs entered captivity, and two peoples inherited a rivalry whose causes reached back to choices made beneath another sky.

outcome.summary: The Alliance defeated the Old Horde, destroyed the original Dark Portal, and imprisoned many surviving orcs; the political and human consequences carried forward toward the Third War.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The Second War spanned land, sea, air, and many engagements. No single battlefield marker or complete exact route is asserted.

battles.name: The Titan-forged War against the Black Empire

date.label: After the titan-forged were mustered

battles.summary: Keeper-led armies of stone and metal fought across primordial Azeroth, defeated the Black Empire's forces, and subdued the powers that had ruled the world.
battles.description: This title groups a world-spanning campaign described across the source account’s Ordering sequence. The sources do not establish a surveyable front or one battle coordinate, so the atlas provides phases without an invented route or marker.

objectives.summary: Break the Black Empire while preserving Azeroth's nascent world-soul.
Hold the Old Gods' dominion against the keeper-led invasion.

phases.title: The keepers lead the hosts
phases.summary: Empowered keepers direct the first titan-forged armies into the corrupted world.
phases.narration: The keepers went before the hosts of living stone and metal. They did not come to conquer a kingdom for themselves, but to reach the power buried beneath it without destroying the world they had been made to save.

phases.title: The elemental powers are subdued
phases.summary: The titan-forged overcome the elemental forces bound to the Old Gods.
phases.narration: Storm, flame, stone, and sea rose against the invaders under the Old Gods' dominion. One by one those ancient powers were overcome, and the keepers prepared realms apart from the waking world in which the elemental hosts could be confined.

phases.title: The citadels are broken
phases.summary: The keeper-led hosts dismantle the Black Empire's military dominion.
phases.narration: Across unnamed fronts, the Black Empire's fortresses and servant hosts yielded. The sources give no single road by which the victory came, only a widening collapse as the titan-forged pressed toward the Old Gods themselves.

phases.title: The surviving Old Gods are bound
phases.summary: The remaining Old Gods are defeated and contained rather than torn from the world.
phases.narration: The lesson of the world-wound could not be ignored. The surviving Old Gods were not pulled free. They were overcome, chained, and sealed beneath Azeroth, so that their roots might remain without tearing the sleeping titan apart.

phases.title: A wounded world remains
phases.summary: Victory ends the empire but leaves a planet requiring containment and repair.
phases.narration: The empire had fallen, yet victory was not wholeness. Prisons lay beneath the earth, a wound burned at the continent's heart, and the keepers turned from war toward the longer labor of making Azeroth stable again.

outcome.summary: The Black Empire's rule was broken; its elemental powers were confined, the surviving Old Gods were imprisoned, and the keepers could begin healing and ordering Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Chronicle describes a world-spanning campaign but does not provide an exact battle site, front line, or campaign route. No marker is asserted.

battles.name: The Troll–Aqir War

date.label: After the aqir awakening

battles.summary: A long, multi-front struggle in which the Empire of Zul resisted the aqir and pursued their retreating forces toward the distant reaches of Kalimdor.
battles.description: This dossier presents strategic phases rather than a tactical simulation. The surviving account supports broad directions and consequences, not a single battlefield path or exact front line.

objectives.summary: Unite the threatened troll peoples, survive the first assault, and drive the aqir away from their centers.
Break the emerging troll powers and spread through their territories.

phases.title: The buried danger returns
phases.summary: Aqir forces emerge and press into the divided lands of the troll peoples.
phases.narration: The first change was not a border but a pressure felt across many lands: an ancient enemy rising beneath a world that had begun to forget it.

phases.title: The trolls unite
phases.summary: Zandalari leadership draws several troll peoples into the Empire of Zul.
phases.narration: Old rivalries did not vanish, yet the threat made alliance possible. The coalition carried many peoples without making them one people.

phases.title: The pursuit crosses Kalimdor
phases.summary: Troll forces pursue the retreating aqir toward northern and southern refuges over generations of war.
phases.narration: The struggle widened beyond any single field. Its roads are represented only in broad direction, for no surviving account measures every march.
