phases.title: One enemy becomes several powers
phases.summary: The aqir threat is broken apart, leaving separated successor populations entrenched at opposite reaches of the continent.
phases.narration: Victory did not empty the earth. It divided an enemy, leaving distant powers whose descendants would trouble later ages.

outcome.summary: The Empire of Zul survived and the aqir were driven into separated refuges; the troll coalition then loosened as its members occupied distant regions.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The conflict was world-spanning and its exact fronts are not reconstructed as a battlefield marker or route.

battles.name: The Troll Wars

date.label: Approximately 2,800 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

battles.summary: A multi-stage war in which the Amani offensive against Quel'Thalas drew the high elves and Arathor into a decisive alliance.
battles.description: This dossier presents the political and strategic sequence rather than exact troop movements. The sources support an assault, alliance, transfer of arcane knowledge, and allied victory, but not a surveyed front line suitable for a single battle marker.

objectives.summary: Break the high-elven occupation and recover control over contested ancestral lands.
Preserve the kingdom and Sunwell against an overwhelming offensive.
Honor the wartime compact and prevent Amani power from threatening the united human nation.

phases.title: The northern war widens
phases.summary: Amani pressure grows into an assault that Quel'Thalas cannot safely contain alone.
phases.narration: The forest war was not born upon an empty map. Two peoples claimed memory in the same northern lands, and the old contest returned with strength enough to threaten the kingdom around the Sunwell.

phases.title: Need makes an alliance
phases.summary: Quel'Thalas seeks Arathor's aid and offers limited arcane instruction in return.
phases.narration: Distance and distrust yielded to necessity. The high elves opened a guarded portion of their learning; Arathor committed the weight of a nation that had only recently learned to stand as one.

phases.title: A new art enters human history
phases.summary: A limited company of humans trained in arcane magic joins the allied campaign.
phases.narration: The exchange outlived the emergency that created it. Fire answered the forest host, and human history acquired a power whose consequences would reach far beyond this war.

phases.title: Two powers converge
phases.summary: High-elven and Arathorian forces combine their strengths against the Amani campaign.
phases.narration: Neither ally fought as an ornament to the other. One brought knowledge of the northern land and arcane war; the other brought numbers, cohesion, and Thoradin's command.

phases.title: Victory changes the north
phases.summary: The allies win decisively and Amani regional power is reduced, though the Amani endure.
phases.narration: The offensive ended in defeat, but not in the disappearance of a people. The Amani endured with memory sharpened by loss, while their victors entered a season of expansion.

outcome.summary: Quel'Thalas and Arathor defeated the immediate Amani campaign; Amani power was greatly reduced, the high-elven kingdom survived, and arcane practice took root among humans.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The war contained several movements and engagements. No single exact battlefield point or tactical route is asserted.

battles.name: The Visions of N'Zoth Campaign

date.label: After N'Zoth's release

battles.summary: A strategic dossier of N'Zoth's assaults, the defense of mind and world, and the campaign into Ny'alotha.

phases.title: The prison opens
phases.summary: N'Zoth's release turns hidden pressure into open assault.
phases.narration: What had whispered beneath history stepped into its open page, and the wounded world found no shelter in disbelief.

phases.title: Assaults fall upon the world
phases.summary: Forces of the Old God attack key regions while corruption spreads through vision and fear.
phases.narration: The assault was made against walls and wills together; the map's violet shadows mark pressure, not measured borders.

phases.title: The defenders learn to endure the visions
phases.summary: Champions prepare to resist corruption while answering the assaults.
phases.narration: To reach the enemy, the defenders first had to carry an answer within themselves.

phases.title: The campaign enters Ny'alotha
phases.summary: The struggle crosses into N'Zoth's terrible domain.
phases.narration: The atlas cannot place that nightmare as an ordinary province. It names the crossing and refuses a false geography.

phases.title: The immediate assault is ended
phases.summary: N'Zoth is defeated and the campaign closes.
phases.narration: The vision broke and the world remained—scarred, uncertain, and soon to face a wound in the boundary of death itself.

outcome.summary: Champions defeated N'Zoth and ended his immediate assault on Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Ny'alotha is not treated as a conventional measured place, and the multi-region campaign has no single exact marker.

battles.name: The War Against the Burning Legion

date.label: From the Broken Isles campaign through Argus

battles.summary: A cross-world strategic dossier from the Legion's return to the coalition's campaign on Argus.
battles.description: This dossier changes worldspaces rather than drawing a false geographic route between Azeroth and Argus.

phases.title: The Legion returns through the Broken Isles
phases.summary: A renewed invasion establishes the Broken Isles as its opening theater.
phases.narration: The old enemy returned not as a rumor of ancient ruin, but as armies beneath a green and wounded sky.

phases.title: The orders answer separately and together
phases.summary: Distinct orders gather champions when familiar institutions cannot carry the whole defense.
phases.narration: Different callings kept their own halls and names, yet turned their strength toward one survival.

phases.title: The Broken Isles campaign opens the way
phases.summary: The defense develops the means to carry the war beyond Azeroth.
phases.narration: Island by island, the defense became an answer bold enough to cross the boundary between worlds.

phases.title: The atlas turns to shattered Argus
phases.summary: The coalition reaches the Legion's ancient seat without a false line between worlds.
phases.narration: No ocean joined these shores. The atlas closes one measure and opens another upon a world long held in ruin.

phases.title: The crusade is broken at its source
phases.summary: The Argus campaign ends the Legion's immediate cosmic crusade.
phases.narration: Upon the broken world, old exiles and new champions carried the war to its source, and an age-long crusade lost the certainty of return.

outcome.summary: The coalition's campaign on Argus broke the Burning Legion's immediate crusade.

battles.geographicEditorNote: This cross-world campaign is deliberately not assigned one geographic marker.

battles.name: The War of the Ancients

date.label: c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal

battles.summary: A continent-spanning war in which the Burning Legion devastated ancient Kalimdor before a changing alliance disrupted the gateway at the Well.
battles.description: This dossier presents five strategic phases rather than a tactical simulation. The invasion crossed many places and involved many participants; the surviving account does not support one exact battlefield marker or a single continuous front line.

objectives.summary: Secure the gateway, destroy resistance across Kalimdor, and enable Sargeras to enter Azeroth.
Sustain and enlarge the portal at the Well in service of Azshara's alliance with the Legion.
Survive the invasion, gather allies, and disrupt the gateway before Sargeras can cross.

phases.title: The court opens the gate
phases.summary: The Highborne channel the Well into a portal and Legion forces enter through Zin-Azshari.
phases.narration: The empire's center became the road of its undoing. From the Well, the invasion widened across lands still joined beneath one sky.

phases.title: A divided people resists
phases.summary: Kaldorei opponents of Azshara organize and converge while the invasion spreads.
phases.narration: There was no single untouched road to victory. Defenders gathered through burning country, carrying different loyalties toward one necessity.

phases.title: The living world enters the war
phases.summary: Cenarius and other ancient powers join the defense while the Dragon Aspects prepare the Dragon Soul.
phases.narration: Forest, wing, and mortal courage stood together, for the Legion's victory would leave no separate realm in which any could endure.

phases.title: The weapon turns upon its makers
phases.summary: Neltharion uses the Dragon Soul against allies as well as enemies, breaking the dragons' unity.
phases.narration: A weapon made by many answered to one corrupted will. In the hour of alliance, betrayal opened another wound within the defense.

phases.title: All roads return to the Well
phases.summary: The defenders converge on the gateway and disrupt it before Sargeras can enter Azeroth.
phases.narration: At last the war returned to the water from which the empire's power had risen. The gate was broken, but the world beneath it could not remain whole.

outcome.summary: The Legion's immediate invasion was stopped and Sargeras did not enter Azeroth, but the Well collapsed and the resulting Sundering destroyed the old continental world.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The war was continent-spanning. Only the Well and Zin-Azshari receive approximate location context; the battle itself has no exact marker.

battles.name: The War of the Three Hammers

date.label: Approximately 230 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

battles.summary: A dwarven succession war drove the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from Ironforge, opened new centers, and ended when Ragnaros's return devastated the southern mountains.
battles.description: The dossier joins two connected phases of civil conflict at strategic scale. It does not treat Ironforge, Grim Batol, the Redridge front, and the volcanic aftermath as one exact battlefield.

objectives.summary: Competing clans sought control, survival, or revenge across Ironforge and the strongholds founded after the first expulsion.

phases.title: One mountain loses its center
phases.summary: The high king's death breaks the balance among the three clans.
phases.narration: A mountain that had contained many loyalties could not contain their claims once its old center failed. Kinship became a line of battle beneath the stone.

phases.title: Ironforge chooses a victor
phases.summary: The Bronzebeards retain the city while the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans are expelled.
phases.narration: Victory kept one clan beneath the mountain and sent two others into landscapes where grievance would harden into new identities.

phases.title: Defeat becomes new kingdoms
phases.summary: The Wildhammers establish Grim Batol while the Dark Irons establish Thaurissan farther south.
phases.narration: Exile did not end either people. New halls rose north and south, and the old quarrel acquired distance without acquiring peace.

phases.title: Revenge opens two fronts
phases.summary: Dark Iron armies strike toward both Ironforge and Grim Batol and are driven back.
phases.narration: The war returned along two roads. Former rivals answered the same danger, and the armies of the deep were broken between the powers they had meant to defeat apart.

phases.title: The earth answers the last summons
phases.summary: A desperate summoning brings Ragnaros into the world and transforms the southern mountains.
phases.narration: At the edge of defeat, a call went downward into powers older than every dwarven throne. The answer ended the war by making the land itself more terrible than victory.

outcome.summary: The Bronzebeards retained Ironforge, the Wildhammers and Dark Irons formed separate centers, and Ragnaros's return devastated the southern mountains and subjected surviving Dark Irons to a new power.

battles.geographicEditorNote: This was a dispersed civil war across multiple strongholds and later fronts; the atlas therefore uses only an inferred dispersal route and approximate place markers.

citations.section: Argus

citations.section: The Betrayal of Neltharion

citations.section: The Rise of the Aspects

citations.section: Coiled Isle and Venomous Abyss
citations.note: The released campaign follows Zul’jarra, her brother, and Ula’tek’s unleashed threat.

citations.section: The Flight of the Draenei
citations.note: First-party summary of the draenei on Draenor, Kil'jaeden's pursuit, manipulation of Ner'zhul and Gul'dan, the draenei war, and the invasion through Medivh's Dark Portal.

citations.section: Weaving the Story
citations.note: Supports the Dragon Isles awakening, the dragonflights' return, and the expeditionary frame.

citations.section: The Library — Tides of Darkness
citations.note: First-party summary of Stormwind's fall, the Alliance of Lordaeron's formation, and its stand in the Second War.

citations.section: Complete the Battle for Azeroth War Campaign
citations.note: Supports faction footholds, the rebellion against Sylvanas, and the conclusion identified as the Fourth War.

citations.section: Ghosts of K’aresh
citations.note: Released K’aresh campaign and Dimensius crisis.

citations.section: Mount Hyjal: In Defense of Nordrassil
citations.note: First-party support for Malfurion calling upon Nordrassil's power to destroy Archimonde and repel the Legion and Scourge. Coalition composition remains cross-checked against the Chronicle research packet.

citations.section: Illidan's Legacy
citations.note: First-party summary of Illidan's Outland campaign, Kil'jaeden's command, the assault on the Frozen Throne, and Arthas's victory at Icecrown.

citations.section: The Fate of Azeroth
citations.note: Supports the Legion invasion, Broken Isles theater, class orders, artifact campaign, and Illidari alliance.

citations.section: The First Emperor: Lei Shen
citations.note: First-party corroboration that Lei Shen united the mogu kings and led the conquest and subjugation of other peoples in ancient Pandaria.

citations.section: Midnight — Voidspire
citations.note: Xal’atath turns the Sunwell into the Darkwell; Alleria and Turalyon vanish into it.

citations.section: Midnight — Darkwell and aftermath
citations.note: The elven coalition, Sylvanas’s intervention, Xal’atath’s retreat, and the Dawnwell.

citations.section: Midnight — opening and Eversong Woods
citations.note: Xal’atath and the Devouring Host attack the Sunwell; defenders force an initial retreat.

citations.section: The Rise of the Aspects
citations.note: First-party corroboration that Aggramar proposed powerful constructs to protect the world-soul, the Pantheon empowered keepers, and those keepers led titan-forged armies against the Black Empire.

citations.section: Bring Down the Warchief
citations.note: Supports devastation in the Vale, joint opposition, and the Siege of Orgrimmar ending Garrosh's rule.

citations.section: Legacy of the Blood Elves
citations.note: First-party web corroboration for the exiled high elves' arrival, Quel'Thalas, the Sunwell, the Amani assault, the Arathor alliance, and the exchange of magical teaching for military aid.

citations.section: Legacy of the Blood Elves
citations.note: First-party support for Arthas's Third War invasion of Quel'Thalas, the kingdom's devastation, and the Sunwell's corruption. It does not support the separate Sylvanas or Forsaken claims.

citations.section: Relive the events of Warcraft III
citations.note: First-party summary of the campaign's geographic and historical scope through the rise of the Lich King.

citations.section: The Library — Rise of the Horde
citations.note: First-party summary of Legion manipulation, Mannoroth's blood, formation of the Horde, and the devastation of the draenei and Draenor.

citations.section: Shadowlands is live
citations.note: Supports Sylvanas piercing the veil and the heroes' journey through the afterlife and Covenant framework.

citations.section: Warcraft III: The Story So Far
citations.note: Broad first-party chronology for the plague, Arthas, Thrall, the Scourge, the Legion, and the night elves; mission-level detail is not inferred from this summary.

citations.section: Arms — Stromkar, the Warbreaker
citations.note: First-party web corroboration that Thoradin united humanity, founded Arathor, and played a critical role in ending the Troll Wars.

citations.section: Cataclysm: Grim Batol — historical introduction
citations.note: First-party web corroboration for the three-clan civil war, the Bronzebeard hold on Ironforge, Wildhammer migration to Grim Batol, Dark Iron settlement at Thaurissan, and their later two-front assault.

citations.section: Visions of N'Zoth
citations.note: Supports N'Zoth's release, assaults, Ny'alotha, and the broad battle for Azeroth's survival.

citations.section: Discover the Land of Khaz Algar
citations.note: Supports Khaz Algar, subterranean theaters, and Xal'atath gathering forces in the opening Worldsoul Saga chapter.

citations.section: Official synopsis and cinematic
citations.note: First-party corroboration that the Sundering tore Azeroth's lands apart and that Azshara and Highborne followers survived beneath the sea through transformation.

citations.section: Warlords of Draenor reveal
citations.note: Supports the alternate Draenor theater, Iron Horde formation, and planned invasion through the Dark Portal.

citations.section: Well of Eternity
citations.note: First-party corroboration for Zin-Azshari at the Well, the Highborne portal, Azshara's command, the final struggle, the Great Sundering, and the creation of the Maelstrom.

citations.section: Icecrown
citations.note: Broad support for the Lich King's command from Icecrown Citadel and the champions' final confrontation.

citations.section: The rise of Arathor and the Troll Wars
citations.note: Working research range for Thoradin's unification, the Amani threat, the Quel'Thalas-Arathor compact, human magi, and the strategic outcome. Exact chronology and phase wording require human review.

citations.section: The Black Empire map
citations.note: Visual cartography reference indexed by Warcraft Wiki; exact placements remain research reconstructions until human review of the edition.

citations.section: Coming of the Old Gods
citations.note: Supports the Old Gods' arrival, the n'raqi and aqir, Y'Shaarj's central bastion, the Black Empire's expansion, and the elementals' united response.

citations.section: Introduction: Cosmology and The Cosmic Forces
citations.note: Supports the cosmic frame and the roles of Light, Shadow/Void, Life, Death, Order, Disorder, and the elements.

citations.section: The Discovery of Azeroth
citations.note: Supports Aggramar's discovery of Azeroth, the Pantheon's recognition of the threatened world-soul, and the decision to intervene. Pagination is indexed for research and requires human confirmation against the selected complete edition.

citations.section: The War of the Ancients — the Dragon Soul and Neltharion's betrayal
citations.note: Working research range for the artifact's creation, its use against the Legion, and Neltharion's attack on his allies. Exact pagination and the artifact's contemporary naming require human confirmation.

citations.section: The Empire of Zul and the Awakening of the Aqir
citations.note: Supports the early troll polities, the Empire of Zul, Kith'ix's awakening, the troll-aqir war, and the aqir retreat toward separate northern and southern strongholds. The official Dark Horse preview supplies this research range; pagination and interpretation require human confirmation.

citations.section: Fall of the Black Empire
citations.note: Supports Y'Shaarj's destruction by Aman'Thul, the catastrophic wound left in Azeroth, and the defeat of the Black Empire. Exact wording and pagination require human review.

citations.section: The War of the Ancients — the Sundering and aftermath
citations.note: Working research range for the portal's collapse, destruction of the Well, the Sundering, the Maelstrom, and survivors reaching the lands around Mount Hyjal. Individual route details and exact pagination require human review.

citations.section: Highborne exile and the founding of Quel'Thalas
citations.note: Working research range for the arcane dispute, exile, eastward migration, Dath'Remar's leadership, the Sunwell, and Quel'Thalas. Exact page-to-claim allocation requires human review.

citations.section: Arathor's expansion and the emergence of the human kingdoms
citations.note: Working research range. The atlas represents a long political fragmentation with broad influence areas, not a single date of simultaneous independence or surveyed borders. Human review must verify the edition and kingdom sequence.

citations.section: The second Well, Nordrassil, Illidan's imprisonment, and the beginning of the Long Vigil
citations.note: Working research range. Exact pagination, the division between immediate aftermath and later institutions, and every blessing attributed to the Aspects require human edition review.

citations.section: The Mogu Empire
citations.note: Supports the mogu's division after Ra's disappearance, Lei Shen's rise, the empire he established in the southern lands, and its systems of conquest. The exact range requires human confirmation against the selected edition.

citations.section: The Well of Eternity and the Rise of the Night Elves; Queen Azshara
citations.note: Supports Chronicle's account of dark trolls settling near the Well, their transformation into the kaldorei, the rapid expansion of their civilization, and Azshara's ascent. Exact section boundary and pagination require human confirmation.

citations.section: The Ordering of Azeroth
citations.note: Supports the keepers' and titan-forged peoples' work shaping mountains, waterways, seas, living enclaves, and the primary continent called Kalimdor. Pagination requires human review.

citations.section: Origins of the Universe
citations.note: Supports Chronicle's account of primordial Light and Void, the birth of the Great Dark Beyond, and the formation of the Twisting Nether. Pagination requires human confirmation against the selected complete edition.

citations.section: The Pandaren Revolution
citations.note: Working research range for Kang's resistance, the wider slave uprising, and the fall of the mogu empire. Exact pagination, named participants, and sequence require human review before promotion.

citations.section: The Pantheon's Departure
citations.note: Supports the Pantheon's departure after leaving Azeroth in the care of its appointed servants and safeguards. Pagination requires human review.

citations.section: Reign of the Elements
citations.note: Supports Azeroth's nascent world-soul, the shortage of Spirit, the four Elemental Lords, and their prolonged shifting conflict.

citations.section: The War of the Three Hammers
citations.note: Working research range for the succession crisis, the three-clan war, expulsion from Ironforge, separate strongholds, renewed Dark Iron attack, and the war's volcanic consequence. Exact pagination and phase boundaries require human review.

citations.section: The Titans
citations.note: Supports the world-soul lifecycle, Aman’Thul's awakening and search, and the gathering and world-ordering purpose of the Pantheon. Pagination requires human confirmation against the selected complete edition.

citations.section: The Void Lords and the Old Gods
citations.note: Supports Chronicle's account of the Void Lords' world-soul objective, their limited manifestation in the physical universe, and the creation and scattering of the Old Gods. Pagination requires human confirmation against the selected complete edition.

citations.section: The War of the Ancients — opening
citations.note: Working research range for Azshara's court, the Highborne's use of the Well, and the opening of the Legion invasion. Exact pagination and section boundary require human confirmation against the selected edition.

citations.section: The War of the Ancients — resistance and allies
citations.note: Working research range for Malfurion, Tyrande, Illidan, Cenarius, the wider resistance, and the joining of ancient allies. Exact page coverage and participant emphasis require human review.

citations.section: The Well of Eternity and the World Forges
citations.note: Supports the Old Gods' imprisonment, the keepers' stabilization of Azeroth's wound into the Well of Eternity, and the complementary world-forge system. Pagination requires human review.

citations.section: Wrath of the Titan-Forged
citations.note: Supports the stone-and-metal titan-forged, the empowered keepers, and their campaign against the Black Empire and its elemental servants. Pagination requires human review.
